ny.title: License Law and Regulations
ny.intro: Who needs a license, what the Department of State (DOS) can do to licensees, and the Part 175 rules you will be tested on most. Almost every number on this page is fair game.

ny.title: Law of Agency
ny.intro: The biggest unit on the syllabus (11 hours). Know who represents whom, the six fiduciary duties, how agency is created and ended, dual agency with designated sales agents, and the §443 disclosure form cold.

ny.title: Legal Issues: Estates, Liens, Deeds, Closings
ny.intro: Four sub-units: Estates & Interests (3 hrs), Liens & Easements (2.5), Deeds (2.5), and Title Closing & Costs (2). This is a heavy vocabulary unit.

ny.title: The Contract of Sales and Leases
ny.intro: Leases (1 hr), contracts (1 hr), and contract preparation (1 hr). Know the essentials of a valid contract, the Statute of Frauds, and NY landlord-tenant rules.

ny.title: Real Estate Finance
ny.intro: Mortgage basics (4 hrs) and predatory lending (1 hr). Know the parties, the clauses, the loan types, the secondary market, Regulation Z's trigger terms, and what lenders look at.

ny.title: Land Use Regulations
ny.intro: How government and private agreements control what can be built. Know the four government powers, variance standards (use vs area), nonconforming uses, and who does what.

ny.title: Construction and Environmental Issues
ny.intro: Construction terms and house systems (2 hrs) and environmental hazards (3 hrs). You don't need to be an inspector. Know the vocabulary, the hazards, and when to recommend a professional.

ny.title: Valuation Process and Pricing Properties
ny.intro: Appraisal vs CMA, the definition of market value, the three approaches to value, and how to price a listing.

ny.title: Human Rights and Fair Housing
ny.intro: Heavily tested and heavily enforced in NY. Know the federal, NY State and NYC protected classes, the exemptions (and who can't use them), the prohibited practices, and the DOS disclosure and posting rules.

ny.title: Real Estate Mathematics
ny.intro: Only 1 hour of class, but math shows up across the exam. Learn these formulas, then drill with the Math tab, which makes unlimited fresh problems.

ny.title: Municipal Agencies
ny.intro: Match each local agency to its job. Exam questions are usually "which board does X?"

ny.title: Property Insurance
ny.intro: The homeowner policy forms, how coverage amounts work, and what an agent should explain to a buyer.

ny.title: Licensee Safety
ny.intro: Common-sense safety for the office, showings, open houses and online. Exam questions usually ask for the safest practice.

ny.title: Taxes and Assessments
ny.intro: How NY property taxes are calculated, how assessments work, exemptions like STAR, and how owners challenge assessments (Grievance → SCAR or certiorari).

ny.title: Condominiums and Cooperatives
ny.intro: Very important in NYC. Know what a condo buyer gets vs a co-op buyer, the documents, board packages, sponsor issues, and how the closing costs differ.

ny.title: Commercial and Investment Properties
ny.intro: A big unit (10 hrs): the math of investment property (NOI, cash flow, cap rates) plus commercial lease vocabulary like escalations, square-footage factors and SNDA clauses.

ny.title: Income Tax Issues in Real Estate Transactions
ny.intro: Federal income tax topics: the home-sale exclusion, deductions, capital gains, depreciation, passive income, and 1031 exchanges. Explain these, but always refer clients to a tax professional.

lessons.title: Income Tax Issues in Real Estate Transactions 1
Income Tax Issues in Real Estate Transactions 2
Income Tax Issues in Real Estate Transactions 3
Income Tax Issues in Real Estate Transactions 4
Income Tax Issues in Real Estate Transactions 5

ny.title: Mortgage Brokerage
ny.intro: Mortgage broker vs mortgage banker, their roles in a deal, and the disclosure licensees need if they wear both hats.

ny.title: Property Management
ny.intro: What property managers do, the management agreement, budgets and maintenance, and their duties to the owner.

us.title: Property Ownership
us.intro: What real property is, how it is owned, and the rights and limits that travel with the land. The exam loves fixtures, concurrent ownership, and the difference between a condo and a co-op.

us.title: Land Use Controls and Regulations
us.intro: How government and private agreements decide what can be built and used. Know the four public powers, zoning tools, and which rule wins when zoning and a deed restriction collide.

us.title: Valuation and Market Analysis
us.intro: How value is estimated for lenders, buyers and sellers. Know the three approaches, the big appraisal principles, and why a CMA is not an appraisal.

us.title: Financing
us.intro: How mortgages work, the loan types you will see on the exam, the secondary market, and the federal rules that govern ads, disclosures and fair lending.

us.title: Agency and Fiduciary Duties
us.intro: Who you represent, the six fiduciary duties, how agency starts and ends, and the listing contracts that create it. Who pays the commission does not decide who the client is.

us.title: Property Disclosures and Environmental Issues
us.intro: What must be told, what is a material fact, and the environmental hazards that show up on the national exam. Federal lead-paint and Superfund rules are fair game; stigmatized-property rules are not the same in every state.

us.title: Contracts
us.intro: What makes a real estate contract valid, how offers live and die, and the remedies when someone breaches. Land is unique, so specific performance is the remedy that shows up on every exam.

us.title: Leasing and Property Management
us.intro: The four leasehold estates, the lease forms that show up on exams, how tenancies end, and the property manager's job as a general agent who handles other people's money.

us.title: Transfer of Title and Closing
us.intro: How title moves: deeds, recording, title insurance, and the closing table. Delivery and acceptance make a deed work; recording protects it against later claims.

us.title: Practice of Real Estate (fair housing, antitrust, advertising, trust funds)
us.intro: How a brokerage must behave: federal fair housing, Sherman Act antitrust rules, truthful advertising, and other people's money. These topics are heavily tested because they are how licenses are lost.

us.title: Real Estate Calculations
us.intro: The math the national exam actually asks: commissions, seller's net, area, loan costs, prorations, taxes, and investment formulas. Read every question for the period, the base (price versus loan), and who owns the day of closing.

u1-1k2rcis.q: What is the minimum age to be licensed as a NY real estate salesperson?
u1-1k2rcis.e: RPL §440-a: a salesperson must be over 18. A broker must be at least 20.

u1-1xphhay.q: What is the minimum age to be licensed as a NY real estate broker?

u1-5m01ap.q: How many hours of approved qualifying education must a salesperson applicant complete?
u1-5m01ap.e: The salesperson qualifying course is 77 hours (plus a school final exam).

u1-36w4c3.q: An applicant for a broker's license must complete a total of how many hours of qualifying education?
u1-36w4c3.e: Brokers need 152 hours: the 77-hour salesperson course plus the 75-hour broker course.

u1-thg5jm.q: A NY real estate license is issued for a term of:
u1-thg5jm.e: RPL §441-a(7): licenses are issued for 2 years.

u1-1hjcg9q.q: How many hours of continuing education must a licensee complete each license term?
u1-1hjcg9q.e: 22.5 hours per 2-year term, including cultural competency, fair housing, implicit bias, ethics, recent legal matters and agency.

u1-ary2mr.q: During a salesperson's FIRST two-year license term, how many hours of agency instruction are required as part of continuing education?
u1-ary2mr.e: RPL §441(3)(a): salespersons need 2 hours of agency in the initial term and 1 hour in later terms.

u1-1br84ao.q: The Department of State may impose a fine on a licensee of up to how much per violation?
u1-1br84ao.e: RPL §441-c: up to $2,000, with half going to the anti-discrimination in housing fund.

u1-d6jbs3.q: After a license is revoked, how long must the person wait before being eligible to be relicensed?
u1-d6jbs3.e: RPL §441-c(4): ineligible for 1 year from the date of revocation.

u1-1ny1tl7.q: A broker receives a buyer's deposit check. Under 19 NYCRR 175.1, it must be deposited into a separate special account:
c: Before the end of the month
u1-1ny1tl7.e: Deposits must go into a separate, special, federally insured account within 3 business days.

u1-f3gw6n.q: Mixing a client's money with the broker's own business or personal funds is called:
u1-f3gw6n.e: Commingling is prohibited (175.1). Conversion is actually using the client's money for yourself.

u1-1ketjuj.q: A salesperson closes a deal and the grateful seller wants to hand the salesperson a $1,000 bonus check directly. The salesperson may:
c: Accept it if the broker is told afterward
Accept compensation only through their sponsoring broker
Accept it only if it is under $500
Accept it because it is a gift
u1-1ketjuj.e: RPL §442-a: a salesperson may receive compensation only from the broker they are associated with.

u1-1opvchf.q: A seller tells the listing broker: "Get me $400,000 net and you can keep anything above that." This arrangement is:
c: A net listing, which is prohibited in NY
u1-1opvchf.e: Net listings are prohibited by 19 NYCRR 175.19.

u1-12468q5.q: Acting as a real estate broker without a license is:
u1-12468q5.e: RPL §442-e: any violation of Article 12-A is a misdemeanor.

u1-9tt46d.q: A person who collected a commission while violating Article 12-A can be sued by an aggrieved party for a penalty of up to:
u1-9tt46d.e: RPL §442-e(3): between 1 and 4 times the amount received.

u1-1pjuhio.q: To sue for a commission in a NY court, the plaintiff must prove they were:
c: A member of a REALTOR association
Licensed on the date the cause of action arose
Licensed for at least two years
u1-1pjuhio.e: RPL §442-d: licensure on the date the claim arose is a prerequisite to suing for compensation.

u1-utrh5z.q: Which of the following may negotiate a real estate sale for another for a fee WITHOUT a real estate license?
c: A person who manages rentals for a neighbor for a fee
u1-utrh5z.e: RPL §442-f exempts attorneys at law, along with court-appointed persons and public officers.

u1-3iw7s9.q: A broker's license is suspended by the Department of State. What happens to the licenses of the salespersons associated with that broker?
c: They are transferred automatically to the office manager
They are suspended until the salespersons associate with another broker (or the suspension ends)
u1-3iw7s9.e: RPL §441-d: the broker's suspension or revocation suspends the associated salespersons' licenses.

u1-5pwld.q: A broker can be disciplined for a salesperson's violation of the license law when the broker:
c: Had actual knowledge of it or kept the benefits after notice of it
Was on vacation when it happened
Did not personally train the salesperson
u1-5pwld.e: RPL §442-c: broker liability requires actual knowledge, or retaining the benefits after notice.

u1-1ksbxq9.q: A salesperson's association with Broker A ends on Friday. On Saturday, before associating with any other broker, the salesperson:
c: May continue working on pending deals
May not perform any licensed activity
May show property but not negotiate
May act as an unlicensed assistant for a commission
u1-1ksbxq9.e: RPL §442-b: after termination, a salesperson may not perform licensed acts until associated with a new broker.

u1-1kr2lcb.q: When a salesperson leaves a brokerage, 19 NYCRR 175.14 requires the salesperson to:
c: Turn over all listing information to the broker
Pay a $20 fee to the broker
u1-1kr2lcb.e: All listing information obtained during the association belongs to the broker and must be turned over.

u1-1x5op1q.q: For how long must a broker keep transaction records for residential sales under 19 NYCRR 175.23?
u1-1x5op1q.e: Transaction records are kept for 3 years.

u1-4akq58.q: An exclusive listing agreement says it "renews automatically for successive 90-day periods unless canceled." This clause is:
c: Allowed if initialed by the seller
u1-4akq58.e: 19 NYCRR 175.15 prohibits automatic continuation beyond the fixed termination date.

u1-1slpo6.q: A broker may place a "For Sale" sign on a property:
c: Whenever it is listed on the MLS
Only after a contract is signed
u1-1slpo6.e: 19 NYCRR 175.11: no sign without the owner's consent.

u1-1jond1e.q: Under DOS advertising rules, which is true about advertisements by a salesperson?
c: A salesperson may advertise any property on the MLS
The ad must include the name of the salesperson's broker or brokerage
A salesperson's ads never need broker approval
Only the salesperson's cell phone may appear
u1-1jond1e.e: 175.25: only the broker places ads, a salesperson needs the broker's approval, and the broker's name must appear.

u1-szeejr.q: Which title is PROHIBITED in NY real estate advertising?
u1-szeejr.e: 175.25(c)(4) prohibits "sales associate," "licensed sales agent," and plain "broker" (for someone who isn't one).

u1-1guenwd.q: Three salespersons at the same firm want to market themselves together. Which name complies with DOS team rules?
c: The Skyline Team at ABC Realty
u1-1guenwd.e: Team names must use the word "team" (not group, realty or associates) and, if members aren't named, add "at/of" the brokerage.

u1-gv3zke.q: An advertisement that does not reveal that the advertiser is a real estate broker is called a:
u1-gv3zke.e: Blind ads are prohibited. Ads must identify the broker or brokerage.

u1-skim7w.q: A licensee who disagrees with a Department of State disciplinary decision may seek court review through:
u1-skim7w.e: RPL §441-f: DOS decisions are reviewable under CPLR Article 78.

u1-mh6xpu.q: A licensee's pocket card must be:
c: Kept by the broker at all times
u1-mh6xpu.e: RPL §441-a(6): pocket cards must be shown on demand.

u1-1xs2ema.q: A licensee convicted of a felony must send DOS a certified copy of the judgment of conviction within how many days of sentencing?
u1-1xs2ema.e: RPL §441-a(12): within 5 days of the imposition of sentence.

u1-1swi4lw.q: The NY Property Condition Disclosure Statement is required in the sale of:
u1-1swi4lw.e: RPL Art. 14 covers 1–4 family dwellings. Condos, co-ops and unimproved land are excluded.

u1-s3utj8.q: Since March 20, 2024, a seller subject to the Property Condition Disclosure Act must:
c: Either deliver the statement or give a $500 credit
Deliver the disclosure statement before the buyer signs a binding contract
Deliver it only if the buyer requests it
u1-s3utj8.e: The 2023 amendment eliminated the $500 credit option. The PCDS must be delivered before the buyer signs the contract.

u1-1cft269.q: A seller's listing agent learns that a death by natural causes occurred in the house last year. Under RPL §443-a, this fact:
c: Must be disclosed in the PCDS
Must be disclosed by the agent orally
Is not a material defect; the buyer may ask in writing and the seller may choose whether to respond
u1-1cft269.e: Deaths, homicides, suicides and felonies on a property are not material defects under §443-a.

u1-197dhcl.q: A seller who knows of uncapped natural gas wells on the property must disclose them:
c: Before entering into a contract of sale
u1-197dhcl.e: RPL §242(3): before entering into a contract.

u1-8njhd8.q: A broker wants to pay a $500 finder's fee to an unlicensed neighbor who referred a buyer. This is:
c: Prohibited: brokers may share commissions only with licensees (or out-of-state brokers)
u1-8njhd8.e: RPL §442 bars paying compensation to unlicensed persons for help with a transaction.

u1-wh4z3a.q: A broker may give part of the commission to the buyer in the transaction as long as:
c: It is not payment for performing licensed activity
It is less than 1% of the price
u1-wh4z3a.e: RPL §442 allows rebates to the parties, as long as they are not compensation for licensed services.

u1-1gi3bl5.q: After a buyer's offer has been accepted, a mortgage broker's friend demands a "referral fee" from the listing broker for sending that buyer. Under RPL §442-l this fee:
c: Is an illegal after-the-fact referral fee absent reasonable cause
Is legal if paid by the seller
u1-1gi3bl5.e: §442-l prohibits after-the-fact referral fees without reasonable cause.

u1-epsqle.q: Under 19 NYCRR 175.21, broker supervision of salespersons must be:
u1-epsqle.e: The regulation requires "regular, frequent and consistent personal guidance, instruction, oversight and superintendence."

c: Voting stock in the brokerage corporation with which they are associated

u1-sinm8z.q: A Florida broker applies for a NY nonresident license. The applicant must file:
c: An irrevocable consent designating the NY Secretary of State to receive service of process
u1-sinm8z.e: RPL §442-g(2) requires an irrevocable consent to service of process.

u1-1esu9cd.q: Before DOS holds a disciplinary hearing, the licensee must receive written notice of the charges at least:
u1-1esu9cd.e: RPL §441-e(2): at least 10 days prior to the hearing.

u1-vdpnzz.q: Which task may an unlicensed assistant perform?
c: Scheduling showing appointments for a licensee
Explaining contract terms to a buyer
u1-vdpnzz.e: Unlicensed assistants may do clerical tasks like scheduling. They may not show, host open houses or negotiate.

u1-ksa0np.q: An applicant has a prior criminal conviction. Under NY law:
c: The conviction is not an automatic bar; DOS evaluates it under Correction Law Article 23-A
u1-ksa0np.e: RPL §440-a refers to Correction Law Article 23-A, which requires an individualized assessment.

u1-k1lodq.q: A broker wants to move the main office across town. The broker must:
c: Get prior approval from the Department of State
u1-k1lodq.e: 19 NYCRR 175.20(d): no relocation without the department's prior approval. Moving without notice suspends the license.

u1-bi27pj.q: A broker's office is on the 12th floor of an office building. The broker's sign requirement is satisfied by:
c: A neon sign in the window
Posting the name and "licensed real estate broker" in the building's directory space
A sign on the broker's car
u1-bi27pj.e: RPL §441-a(3): in office, apartment or hotel buildings, post in the space provided for occupants' names.

u1-1b48wnx.q: How much is the fee for an initial salesperson license (including the fair-housing surcharge)?
u1-1b48wnx.e: $55 plus a $10 surcharge = $65. The exam is $15; a broker license is $185.

u1-1430pik.q: A salesperson changes sponsoring brokers. The fee to file the new record of association is:

u2-1wxo3i4.q: Which is NOT one of the fiduciary duties listed on the NY agency disclosure form?
u2-1wxo3i4.e: The six duties are reasonable care, undivided loyalty, confidentiality, full disclosure, obedience, and duty to account.

u2-1h67ikh.q: A listing expires without a sale. The former listing agent later works with a buyer interested in the same property. The agent:
c: Must still keep the former client's confidential information private
May reveal the seller's lowest acceptable price
May share confidential information after 30 days
Must represent the former seller again
u2-1h67ikh.e: The duty of confidentiality survives the end of the agency.

u2-12evqyy.q: In a seller-agency relationship, the buyer who is not represented is the agent's:
u2-12evqyy.e: The client (principal) is owed fiduciary duties. A customer is owed honesty and fair dealing.

u2-t2epm3.q: A broker hired to find a buyer for one specific house is what type of agent?
u2-t2epm3.e: A listing broker is a special agent, authorized for one specific task.

u2-10jzzfm.q: A property manager who handles leasing, rent collection and maintenance for an owner is usually what type of agent?
u2-10jzzfm.e: Property managers are general agents with broad authority in one area.

u2-1yv6ha9.q: In a typical listing, the salesperson who takes the listing is the:
c: Agent of the broker and subagent of the seller
u2-1yv6ha9.e: The broker is the seller's agent. The salesperson acts for the broker and is the seller's subagent.

u2-ze1ufi.q: An agency relationship created by the words and actions of the parties, without a formal agreement, is:

u2-1pu8r3j.q: A salesperson, without authority, negotiates a deal for an owner. The owner later accepts the benefits of the deal. Agency has been created by:
u2-1pu8r3j.e: Ratification is approving an unauthorized act after the fact.

u2-113re49.q: An owner lets a third party reasonably believe that a person is the owner's agent, and the third party relies on it. The owner may be bound by agency by:
u2-113re49.e: Estoppel keeps the principal from denying an agency its conduct created.

u2-1ke2qd3.q: A buyer's agent will be paid out of the listing broker's commission. Whom does the buyer's agent represent?
c: The seller, because the seller pays
u2-1ke2qd3.e: Who pays does not determine who is represented.

u2-nmk1v2.q: An agency relationship terminates automatically upon:
c: The listing being entered into the MLS
u2-nmk1v2.e: Death or incapacity of either party, destruction of the property, and similar events end the agency.

u2-pro598.q: Two competing brokers agree that neither will charge less than 6%. This is:
u2-pro598.e: Agreeing on commission rates is price fixing under the Sherman Act.

u2-1cowb3b.q: Several brokers agree not to cooperate with a new discount brokerage. This is:
u2-1cowb3b.e: A group boycott is a concerted refusal to deal.

u2-4hb03y.q: Two brokers agree that one will work only north of Main Street and the other only south. This is:
u2-4hb03y.e: Dividing territories or customers among competitors is market allocation.

u2-1aml5tg.q: A developer says, "I'll sell you this lot only if you agree to list your current home with my brokerage." This is:
u2-1aml5tg.e: Conditioning one product or service on buying another is a tie-in.

u2-171vck5.q: Dual agency in NY is permitted only if:
c: The broker discloses it at closing
The broker splits the commission equally
Both parties give informed consent in writing
u2-171vck5.e: Dual agency requires the informed written consent of both buyer and seller (or landlord and tenant).

u2-373g3n.q: A broker represents a buyer and, without telling anyone, also takes a fee from the seller. Possible consequences include:
c: Loss of commission, rescission of the deal, and license discipline
u2-373g3n.e: Undisclosed dual agency is illegal and can cost the commission, the deal and the license.

u2-1u47ayb.q: In a dual agency with designated sales agents, who is the dual agent?
u2-1u47ayb.e: The broker remains the dual agent; designated salespersons advocate for each side.

u2-1wo999t.q: A designated sales agent representing the buyer in an in-house transaction:
c: Advocates for the buyer but cannot provide undivided loyalty
u2-1wo999t.e: Designated sales agents function as advocates, but like the dual agent they cannot provide undivided loyalty.

u2-glnvb6.q: A seller has no vicarious liability for the acts of which cooperating agent?
u2-glnvb6.e: A broker's agent has no direct relationship with the seller. The listing agent who engaged it bears the liability.

u2-1v3zmj8.q: Why might a seller be vicariously liable for the misrepresentations of a cooperating broker?
c: Because every cooperating broker is a buyer's agent
Because the seller paid the MLS fee
Because the cooperating broker was acting as the seller's subagent
u2-1v3zmj8.e: Subagents act for the seller, so the seller can be vicariously liable.

u2-oqde5t.q: The RPL §443 agency disclosure requirements apply to:
c: Sales and rentals of 1–4 family homes and condo/co-op units
u2-oqde5t.e: §443 applies to residential real property: 1–4 family dwellings and condo and co-op units, for sales and rentals.

u2-1ba2rbk.q: A listing agent must give the seller the §443 agency disclosure form:
c: Prior to entering into the listing agreement

u2-uqxcwn.q: A seller's agent must give the §443 disclosure form to a prospective buyer:
c: After the buyer's offer is accepted
At the time of the first substantive contact
u2-uqxcwn.e: §443(3)(b): at the first substantive contact with the buyer.

u2-1syd7qf.q: A buyer refuses to sign the acknowledgment on the §443 form. The agent must:
c: Have the broker sign for the buyer
Prepare a written declaration of the facts under oath or affirmation and keep it at least 3 years

u2-xdf2u6.q: How long must an agent keep a signed §443 acknowledgment?

u2-1awiz3l.q: The NY agency disclosure form states that it:
c: Obligates the buyer to use the agent
u2-1awiz3l.e: It says "THIS IS NOT A CONTRACT."

u2-1gdezf7.q: An owner lists with Broker A under an exclusive right to sell. The owner's cousin buys the house without any broker involvement. Who is owed a commission?
u2-1gdezf7.e: Under an exclusive right to sell, the broker is paid no matter who finds the buyer.

u2-7rnp6g.q: Under an exclusive agency listing, the owner owes NO commission if:
c: A cooperating broker finds the buyer
The property sells above list price
The listing broker finds the buyer
The owner personally finds the buyer
u2-7rnp6g.e: The exclusive agency listing lets the owner sell without a commission.

u2-mdhhv3.q: An owner gives open listings to three brokers. Which broker earns the commission?
c: The broker who is the procuring cause of the sale
None, because open listings are illegal
u2-mdhhv3.e: Open listings pay only the broker who procures the buyer.

u2-2eaua2.q: A seller's agent knows the roof leaks, and the seller asks the agent not to mention it. The agent should:
c: Disclose the known material defect to buyers
u2-2eaua2.e: Agents must disclose known facts that materially affect value or desirability. Obedience doesn't extend to concealment.

u2-18awk8j.q: An agent says a house has "the most charming kitchen in the county." This statement is most likely:
u2-18awk8j.e: Puffing is an obvious opinion or exaggeration, not a statement of fact.

u2-uybsn9.q: A landlord tells the leasing agent not to rent to families with young children. The agent should:
c: Follow the instruction under the duty of obedience
Follow it only for older buildings
Refuse, because the instruction is illegal
u2-uybsn9.e: The duty of obedience covers only lawful instructions. Familial status is protected.

u2-17wrk7h.q: A seller's agent holds the buyer's earnest money deposit. Which fiduciary duty governs handling it properly?
u2-17wrk7h.e: The duty to account covers safeguarding and accounting for money and property.

u2-8gf8bi.q: A buyer asks the seller's agent, "What's the lowest price the seller will take?" The seller's agent should:
c: Disclose the bottom line to keep things moving
u2-8gf8bi.e: The seller's bottom line is confidential information.

u2-1og3xpx.q: After an offer is accepted but before contract, a seller's agent receives a second, higher offer. The agent should:
c: Give it to the first buyer
u2-1og3xpx.e: Full disclosure requires presenting offers to the client unless the client has given other written instructions.

u2-rku5iu.q: Which is a key requirement for a salesperson to be treated as an independent contractor for federal tax purposes (IRC §3508)?
c: They are paid an hourly wage
They are paid a salary with a bonus
They work only from the broker's office
Substantially all pay is tied to sales or output, not hours
u2-rku5iu.e: §3508 requires a license, pay tied to output, and a written contract.

u2-1lw763r.q: Along with being licensed and paid based on output, IRC §3508 requires:
c: A written contract stating the salesperson won't be treated as an employee for tax purposes

u2-12if0ka.q: If salespersons are reclassified as employees, the broker becomes responsible for:
c: Withholding taxes, unemployment insurance, workers' comp and disability
u2-12if0ka.e: Employee status brings payroll tax, unemployment, workers' comp and disability obligations.

u2-qgqgx5.q: An agreement in which a buyer hires a broker to locate property and represent the buyer is often called:
u2-qgqgx5.e: A buyer agency agreement is often styled an exclusive right to represent.
