c: Interstate Land Sales Full Disclosure Act
u102-m1apln.e: The ADA requires reasonable modifications and accessibility in public accommodations and commercial facilities. Fair housing laws address dwellings; the ADA is broader for public spaces.

u102-1h3f6vz.q: Rezoning a parcel from multifamily to single-family, reducing what may be built, is:
c: A taking that always requires payment
u102-1h3f6vz.e: Downzoning is a change to a less intensive classification. Ordinary downzoning under the police power does not by itself require compensation.

u102-2w4vbr.q: Authority for cities and counties to adopt zoning usually comes from:
c: Enabling acts of the state legislature
u102-2w4vbr.e: States delegate police power to local governments through enabling statutes. Local zoning that exceeds that grant can be struck down.

u102-1gd8qis.q: Requests for variances are commonly heard by the:
c: City council sitting as a lender
u102-1gd8qis.e: A board of adjustment or zoning board of appeals is the usual body for variances and many special-exception appeals.

u102-1wbv0fb.q: Combining lots and relaxing some lot-line rules so houses are grouped and open space is preserved is:
u102-1wbv0fb.e: Cluster (density) zoning allows more flexible siting at the same overall density, often to keep common open space.

u102-1yw0rzl.q: Before a new house may be built, the owner generally must obtain a:
u102-1yw0rzl.e: A building permit is required before construction so plans can be checked against codes. The certificate of occupancy comes after the work is approved.

u102-14ymh8h.q: A long-unused nonconforming store is boarded up for many years. The right to resume that use is often lost by:
u102-14ymh8h.e: Nonconforming-use rights can be lost if the use is abandoned or the structure is destroyed, depending on local rules. Mere ownership does not keep an unused illegal-today use alive.

u103-kpwszn.q: Market value is best described as:
c: The price a buyer actually paid last month
The most probable price in an open, arm's-length sale
The assessed value on the tax roll
The cost to rebuild plus land
u103-kpwszn.e: Market value is an opinion of the most probable price a property should bring under normal conditions: willing, informed parties, reasonable exposure, and no undue pressure. Market price is what was actually paid.

u103-glpiwz.q: A comparative market analysis prepared by a licensee differs from an appraisal because a CMA is:
c: Governed by USPAP in every state
A substitute for a certified appraisal in a federally related loan
A marketing tool, not an appraisal
Always identical to the cost approach
u103-glpiwz.e: Licensees use CMAs to help price listings and offers. Appraisals for federally related transactions must be done by credentialed appraisers following USPAP.

u103-cberyv.q: The appraisal principle that a buyer will pay no more than the cost of an equally desirable substitute is:
u103-cberyv.e: Substitution underpins the sales-comparison approach. If two similar houses are available, the lower-priced one tends to set the value of the other.

u103-16pm99b.q: The most profitable legally permitted, physically possible, and financially feasible use is the property's:
u103-16pm99b.e: Highest and best use is the foundation of market-value appraisal. It can be the current use or a different use if conversion is realistic.

u103-128jj7p.q: Combining two adjacent lots so that the whole is worth more than the lots separately illustrates:
u103-128jj7p.e: Assemblage is the act of combining parcels. Plottage is the value increase that results.

u103-ypft0t.q: A modest cottage is surrounded by much larger, more expensive houses. The cottage's value may be pulled up by:
u103-ypft0t.e: Progression is the benefit a lesser property receives from higher-value surroundings. Regression is the opposite effect on a better property in a weaker neighborhood.

u103-1q2l4n7.q: An overimproved house that costs more to upgrade than the value added demonstrates:
u103-1q2l4n7.e: Improvements add value only up to a point. Beyond that, extra dollars do not increase market value dollar-for-dollar.

u103-1gan9v6.q: In the sales-comparison approach, adjustments are made:
c: To the comparable sales, never to the subject
To the subject property's list price
Only to the cost of reproduction
u103-1gan9v6.e: The subject is the property being valued and is not adjusted. Comparables are adjusted to reflect how they differ from the subject.

u103-1p9v710.q: A comparable sold for $412,000 and has a fireplace worth $8,000 that the subject lacks. The adjusted sale price is:
u103-1p9v710.e: If the comparable is better than the subject, subtract the extra feature: $412,000 − $8,000 = $404,000. Remember CBS (comp better, subtract) and CIA (comp inferior, add).

u103-15fbq71.q: The cost approach is often most useful for:
c: A 20-year-old tract house with many comps
A downtown apartment building bought for income
A public library or a new church
A vacant lot with three recent sales
u103-15fbq71.e: Special-purpose properties with few comparable sales and little income are valued by estimating land value plus cost new less depreciation.

u103-1hrk2vm.q: The cost of building an exact replica of an improvement using the same materials and design is:
u103-1hrk2vm.e: Reproduction cost is an exact duplicate. Replacement cost is a building of similar utility with modern materials and design.

u103-1yilyid.q: Worn carpet and a leaking roof are examples of:
u103-1yilyid.e: Physical deterioration is wear and tear or damage to the structure. It may be curable or incurable depending on whether repair is economically justified.

u103-1bo5rkc.q: A four-bedroom house with only one bathroom is most clearly an example of:
u103-1bo5rkc.e: Functional obsolescence is a loss from outdated design or poor layout inside the property. Extra baths would be needed to match market expectations.

u103-l5y3fw.q: A house next to a noisy interstate loses value because of:
u103-l5y3fw.e: External obsolescence arises from causes outside the property line. It is generally incurable because the owner cannot fix the highway.

u103-1a9h6wu.q: An income property has NOI of $48,000. If the market capitalization rate is 8%, indicated value is:
u103-1a9h6wu.e: Value = NOI ÷ cap rate. $48,000 ÷ 0.08 = $600,000. A higher cap rate would produce a lower value.

u103-vaupcq.q: Net operating income is calculated by subtracting operating expenses from effective gross income. Which item is NOT an operating expense for this purpose?
u103-vaupcq.e: NOI is before financing. Mortgage payments and income taxes are not operating expenses in the capitalization formula.

u103-1efan0u.q: A duplex sold for $360,000 and rents for $3,000 per month. The monthly gross rent multiplier is:
u103-1efan0u.e: Monthly GRM = sale price ÷ monthly rent. $360,000 ÷ $3,000 = 120. Value of a similar property ≈ GRM × its monthly rent.

u103-71wx6x.q: Using a GRM of 110, a house that rents for $2,000 per month has an indicated value of:
u103-71wx6x.e: Value = GRM × monthly rent = 110 × $2,000 = $220,000. GRM is a rough income method often used on small residential rentals.

u103-1sxl0qm.q: A property produces $42,000 NOI and sold for $525,000. The overall cap rate is:

u103-9usngd.q: Replacement cost new is $350,000, accrued depreciation is $70,000, and land value is $80,000. Cost-approach value is:
u103-9usngd.e: Cost approach: cost new − depreciation + land. $350,000 − $70,000 + $80,000 = $360,000. Land is not depreciated.

u103-e5a0po.q: After completing the cost, sales-comparison, and income approaches, the appraiser's final step is to:
c: Average the three indicated values equally in every assignment
Report only the highest indicated value
Ignore USPAP if the indications differ
Reconcile the indications by weighting each approach for reliability
u103-e5a0po.e: Reconciliation is professional judgment, not a simple average. A house with good comps may be weighted toward sales comparison; an apartment toward income.

u103-zcmbj4.q: The age a building appears to be, based on condition and utility, is its:
u103-zcmbj4.e: Chronological age is actual years since construction. Effective age reflects upkeep and remodeling. Remaining economic life is how long the improvement is expected to remain useful.

u103-1ptkbi0.q: For most federally related residential loans, appraisal practice is governed by:
u103-1ptkbi0.e: USPAP (Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice) is the national standard. FIRREA requires state-licensed or certified appraisers for covered transactions.

c: An appraisal that always meets USPAP for a federally related loan
A substitute for a home inspection
A value estimate a licensee may prepare for a lender or relocation company, subject to state rules
u103-kost62.e: BPOs and CMAs are not appraisals. States regulate when licensees may prepare them. They do not replace a USPAP appraisal when one is required.

u104-1vgb62f.q: The instrument that is the borrower's personal promise to repay the debt is the:
u104-1vgb62f.e: The note is evidence of the debt. The mortgage or deed of trust is the security instrument that hypothecates the property.

u104-17177d6.q: Pledging real property as security while retaining possession is:
u104-17177d6.e: Hypothecation lets the borrower keep and use the property while it secures the loan. Title and lien theory describe who holds legal title during the loan.

u104-xi3egq.q: In a lien-theory state, during the life of the loan legal title is held by the:
u104-xi3egq.e: Lien theory treats the mortgage as a lien; the borrower keeps title. In title-theory states the lender or a trustee holds title until payoff.

u104-1n1g71p.q: A fully amortized loan is one in which:
c: The balance is zero at the end of the term if all payments are made
Only interest is paid until a balloon is due
The payment covers taxes and insurance only
u104-1n1g71p.e: Each level payment covers interest and a growing share of principal so the loan is paid off at the last payment. A balloon loan is only partly amortized.

u104-91oo5x.q: Private mortgage insurance on a conventional loan is generally required when the LTV is:
u104-91oo5x.e: Conventional lenders typically require PMI above 80% LTV. VA loans use a funding fee and a guaranty rather than PMI. FHA loans use MIP.

u104-n785r1.q: Under the Homeowners Protection Act, a servicer must automatically terminate PMI when the loan reaches:
c: 90% of original value if the borrower asks
78% of the original value, if the borrower is current
u104-n785r1.e: Automatic termination is at 78% of the original value on a current loan. The borrower may request cancellation at 80% of original value if otherwise eligible.

u104-1yiwvs2.q: An FHA loan is best described as a loan that is:
c: Made directly by HUD to the borrower
Guaranteed 100% by the Department of Veterans Affairs
Purchased only by Ginnie Mae at origination
Insured by the Federal Housing Administration
u104-1yiwvs2.e: FHA insures private lenders against loss. Typical low-down-payment FHA purchase programs require an upfront and annual MIP.

u104-1nhcun2.q: A VA-guaranteed purchase loan for an eligible veteran commonly features:
c: Zero down payment and no monthly PMI
Interest-only payments for 30 years by regulation
u104-1nhcun2.e: Eligible veterans may finance 100% of the reasonable value. VA guarantees a portion of the loan; a funding fee usually applies, but PMI is not used.

u104-hxjru6.q: One discount point charged on a $180,000 loan equals:
u104-hxjru6.e: One point is 1% of the loan amount, not of the price. 0.01 × $180,000 = $1,800. Points are prepaid interest that may lower the note rate.

u104-17lphst.q: A buyer pays $400,000 for a house appraised at $400,000 and borrows $320,000. The LTV is:
u104-17lphst.e: LTV = loan ÷ lesser of sale price or appraised value. $320,000 ÷ $400,000 = 80%.

u104-zecanw.q: Interest-only monthly payment on a $240,000 loan at 6% annual interest is:
u104-zecanw.e: Annual interest = $240,000 × 0.06 = $14,400. Monthly = $14,400 ÷ 12 = $1,200. An interest-only (straight) loan does not reduce principal.

u104-1artni5.q: A clause that makes the entire loan balance due if the borrower sells the property is the:
u104-1artni5.e: Due-on-sale (alienation) lets the lender call the loan on transfer. Acceleration calls the balance on default. Defeasance requires the lender to release the lien when the debt is paid.

u104-1gdjd3e.q: If the borrower defaults, the clause that lets the lender declare the whole debt due at once is:
u104-1gdjd3e.e: Acceleration is the lender's remedy after default and is a usual first step toward foreclosure. Prepayment addresses early payoff.

u104-hccsvb.q: A buyer takes title subject to an existing loan but does not sign a note. Who remains personally liable to the lender?
c: Both equally by operation of law
No one, because the lien is void
u104-hccsvb.e: Taking title subject to a mortgage means the buyer does not assume personal liability. The original borrower remains on the note; the lender can still foreclose the property.

u104-1fqaxq3.q: The borrower's right to stop a foreclosure by paying the full amount due before the sale is:
c: Statutory redemption after every sale in all states
u104-1fqaxq3.e: Equitable redemption exists before the foreclosure sale. Statutory redemption, where a state provides it, is a limited period after the sale. Rules vary by state.

u104-11l9v4x.q: A loan covering several parcels that includes a partial-release clause is a:
u104-11l9v4x.e: Developers use blanket mortgages so individual lots can be released as they are sold. A package mortgage covers real and personal property together.

u104-c1l09v.q: A loan that finances both a furnished cabin and the furniture inside it is a:
u104-c1l09v.e: A package loan includes real property and personal property in one security instrument, common with furnished units.

u104-e2adn3.q: A homeowner age 62 or older who wants to convert home equity into cash without a monthly repayment is a typical candidate for a:
u104-e2adn3.e: A reverse mortgage, including FHA's HECM, pays the senior borrower and is usually repaid when the borrower dies, sells, or permanently moves out.

u104-xgcbou.q: For a consumer-purpose dwelling loan, Regulation Z of the Truth in Lending Act requires disclosure of the:
u104-xgcbou.e: TILA/Reg Z tells the consumer the true cost of credit, including the annual percentage rate. It also polices advertising of closed-end dwellings. Business-purpose loans are generally outside Reg Z.

u104-13r3jw8.q: A refinance of a principal dwelling generally gives the borrower a right of rescission of:
c: No rescission; rescission is only for purchases
u104-13r3jw8.e: Reg Z's cooling-off right is three business days for most refinances and home-equity loans on a principal dwelling. It does not apply to a purchase-money loan to buy the home.

u104-1tnxe7w.q: An advertisement that states a specific monthly payment must also disclose other credit terms because that figure is a:
u104-1tnxe7w.e: Trigger terms include the amount or percent of down payment, number or period of payments, the amount of any payment, and the amount of any finance charge. Using one requires full Reg Z advertising disclosures.

c: Payment of a lawful commission to a licensed broker
A Loan Estimate within three business days
Kickbacks and unearned fees for settlement-service referrals
u104-caomaj.e: Section 8 bans giving or receiving a thing of value for the referral of settlement business on a federally related mortgage. Affiliated-business arrangements must be disclosed.

u104-1em2qwy.q: On a closed-end purchase loan covered by TRID, the Closing Disclosure must be received by the borrower at least:
c: Seven calendar days after application only
At the closing table with no prior delivery
u104-1em2qwy.e: TRID combines TILA and RESPA disclosures. The Loan Estimate is due within three business days after application; the Closing Disclosure is due three business days before closing.

u104-4yzn0f.q: The Equal Credit Opportunity Act makes it illegal to discriminate in credit because of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age, or:
c: The applicant's credit score being too low
Collateral that cannot support the loan
The fact that some or all of the applicant's income is from public assistance
u104-4yzn0f.e: ECOA (Regulation B) protects those bases, including receipt of public-assistance income. A lender may still deny credit for legitimate underwriting reasons such as inability to repay.

u105-13q4q93.q: The party a licensee represents and to whom fiduciary duties are owed is the:
u105-13q4q93.e: The client or principal hires the agent. A customer is an unrepresented third party who is still owed honesty and fair dealing.

u105-a0mib5.q: A broker hired to sell one house is acting as a:
c: General agent for all of the seller's affairs
u105-a0mib5.e: A special agent is authorized for a specific transaction or act. Listing and buyer-broker relationships are typically special agency.

u105-a1x734.q: A property manager who collects rents, signs leases, and orders repairs for an owner on an ongoing basis is usually a:
u105-a1x734.e: General agency covers a range of acts in an ongoing business, which is why property managers are the classic example. Universal agency requires very broad power of attorney.

u105-27yrc1.q: An agency created by the parties' spoken or written words is:
u105-27yrc1.e: Express agency is created by agreement, oral or written. Implied agency arises from conduct. Many states require a written listing before a commission can be sued for.

u105-w41cro.q: An owner accepts the benefits of a sale a licensee negotiated without prior authority. Agency may be created by:
u105-w41cro.e: Ratification is after-the-fact approval of an unauthorized act. Estoppel bars a principal from denying an agency that the principal's conduct led others to rely on.

u105-10a7s0k.q: Which listing entitles the broker to a commission no matter who finds the buyer during the listing term?
u105-10a7s0k.e: Exclusive right to sell protects the listing broker even if the seller or another licensee produces the buyer. Exclusive agency lets the seller avoid the commission by selling independently.

u105-st7wox.q: Under an exclusive-agency listing, the seller owes no commission if:
c: The listing broker finds the buyer
A cooperating broker finds the buyer
The seller personally finds the buyer without broker aid
u105-st7wox.e: Exclusive agency gives one broker the exclusive right to market, but the owner may sell on their own and pay nothing. That is the difference from exclusive right to sell.

u105-abwhs2.q: An open listing is one in which:
c: The seller may hire many brokers; only the procuring cause earns a commission
The listing broker is paid even if the seller finds the buyer
Net proceeds above a set price always go to the broker
u105-abwhs2.e: Open listings are nonexclusive. Procuring cause—the unbroken chain of events that leads to the sale—decides who is paid.

u105-71qgaf.q: A listing that promises the broker all proceeds above a net figure to the seller is a net listing. Such listings are:
c: Illegal or strongly discouraged in many states because of the conflict of interest
The only way to list commercial land
Identical to exclusive right to sell
u105-71qgaf.e: The broker's incentive is to underprice the seller's net. Many states ban net listings; elsewhere they are treated as a serious risk.

u105-1pk8i98.q: A seller's broker shares the listing commission with a licensee who is working with the buyer. That payment, standing alone:
c: Makes the licensee the seller's agent as a matter of law
Forbids the licensee from representing the buyer
Does not determine whom the licensee represents
Automatically creates an illegal net listing
u105-1pk8i98.e: Agency is created by agreement and conduct, not by the source of compensation. A buyer's agent may be paid from the listing side and still owe fiduciary duties to the buyer.

u105-1v6b58j.q: The fiduciary duty that requires the agent to put the client's interests above anyone else's, including the agent's, is:
u105-1v6b58j.e: Loyalty is the core fiduciary duty. It forbids self-dealing and secret profits. Obedience applies only to lawful instructions.

u105-1q1wts1.q: After a listing expires, the former listing agent must still protect the seller's:
c: Duty of obedience on new offers
Right to a new free listing
Claim to the next buyer's deposit
u105-1q1wts1.e: Confidentiality survives termination of the agency. Other duties such as obedience and loyalty generally end when the relationship ends, except as to secrets already learned.

u105-1991luk.q: Earnest money mixed into the broker's operating account is:
c: Conversion if later spent on rent
u105-1991luk.e: Commingling is mixing trust funds with broker funds. Conversion is using trust money for the broker's own purposes. Both are grounds for discipline.

u105-9hr9kx.q: Using a client's deposit to pay the brokerage electric bill is:
u105-9hr9kx.e: Conversion is misappropriation of funds held in trust. It is more serious than merely mixing accounts.

u105-a5rdli.q: An agent must obey a client's instructions unless those instructions:
u105-a5rdli.e: Obedience is limited to lawful directions. An agent may not follow orders to conceal a material defect or to discriminate.

u105-w2meto.q: Exaggerated opinions such as calling a small garden a private park are usually:
c: Fraud as a matter of law
u105-w2meto.e: Puffing is sales talk not meant as a statement of fact. A false statement of a material fact is misrepresentation; if intentional, it is fraud.

u105-rsb09d.q: A known hidden (latent) defect that a buyer would not reasonably discover must be:
c: Kept confidential as a seller secret in all cases
Disclosed only if the listing is exclusive
u105-rsb09d.e: Material latent defects known to the agent or seller generally must be disclosed. An as-is clause does not hide known defects. Patent defects are visible on ordinary inspection.

u105-1yq7y3n.q: Competing brokers agree that none will charge less than 6%. This is:
u105-1yq7y3n.e: Commission rates are always negotiable. An agreement among competitors to set rates is criminal and civil antitrust price-fixing.

u105-dv4pvw.q: Several firms refuse to show listings of a new discount brokerage. That concerted refusal is:
u105-dv4pvw.e: A group boycott is a concerted refusal to deal with a competitor. Each firm may set its own policies, but they may not combine to drive another firm out.

u105-jvvqz0.q: Two brokers agree that one will handle only listings west of the highway and the other only east. This is:
c: Legal if they put it in the MLS
u105-jvvqz0.e: Dividing geographic markets or customer classes among competitors is market allocation, another per se antitrust violation.

u105-yvjf28.q: A builder will sell a lot only if the buyer lists the buyer's present house with the builder's brokerage. This is:
u105-yvjf28.e: A tying arrangement conditions the sale of one product or service on the purchase of another. Antitrust law treats coercive tie-ins as unlawful.

u105-b3qidv.q: Representing both buyer and seller in the same transaction without the required consent is:
c: Undisclosed dual agency, which is illegal
u105-b3qidv.e: Dual agency, where allowed, requires informed consent, usually in writing. Hidden dual agency is a breach of loyalty and can cost the commission, the contract, and the license.

u105-zqp18f.q: Death of the principal or of the broker, destruction of the property, and expiration of the listing all:
c: Convert the listing to an open listing
Transfer the listing to the salesperson personally
Have no effect if the house is in escrow
u105-zqp18f.e: Agency also ends by performance, mutual agreement, revocation or renunciation, and often by bankruptcy. Death of a salesperson does not by itself end the broker's listing.

u105-1lfv76x.q: Most salespersons work as independent contractors, but the broker must still:
c: Withhold income tax in every state by federal rule
Avoid any supervision to keep the IRS classification
Pay overtime under the listing contract
Supervise licensed activity as required by license law
u105-1lfv76x.e: IRS independent-contractor treatment and real-estate license-law supervision can coexist. The broker remains responsible for the firm's licensed acts.

u106-pv051d.q: Federal lead-based paint disclosure rules apply to most housing built:
u106-pv051d.e: HUD and EPA rules cover target housing constructed before 1978. Sellers and landlords must disclose known lead-based paint and give the prescribed pamphlet.

u106-ir8qqp.q: Buyers of pre-1978 housing must be given a lead-inspection opportunity of at least:
c: Ten days, unless they waive it in writing
u106-ir8qqp.e: The buyer has a 10-day (or otherwise agreed) chance to inspect for lead. The seller need not test or abate; the buyer may waive the contingency.

u106-mz1o6.q: Which pamphlet must be given to buyers and tenants of most pre-1978 dwellings?
c: Protect Your Family From Lead in Your Home
u106-mz1o6.e: The EPA/HUD pamphlet is a required part of the lead disclosure package, along with any reports the seller has and a lead warning statement in the contract.

u106-dtj5zr.q: Radon is best described as a:
c: Colorless, odorless radioactive gas that can cause lung cancer
Friable mineral fiber used in old insulation
u106-dtj5zr.e: Radon comes from the natural decay of uranium in soil and rock. It enters buildings through foundation cracks. The EPA action level is 4 picocuries per liter.

u106-1bth2zb.q: The EPA recommends radon mitigation when indoor tests are at or above:
u106-1bth2zb.e: Four picocuries per liter is the EPA action level. Mitigation often uses sub-slab depressurization to vent gas outdoors. Tests are commonly taken in the lowest livable area.

u106-11sb03s.q: Asbestos is most dangerous to occupants when it is:
c: Sealed behind intact walls and left undisturbed
Friable and able to release fibers into the air
Used only as vinyl floor tile that is in good condition
u106-11sb03s.e: Friable asbestos can be crumbled by hand and inhaled. Encapsulation or enclosure is often preferred to removal, which can spread fibers if done poorly.

u106-7czl3a.q: A common method of managing intact asbestos without ripping it out is:
c: Flooding the site under CERCLA first
A Phase II soil-gas survey only
u106-7czl3a.e: Encapsulation seals the material so fibers cannot become airborne. Removal is used when the material is damaged or will be disturbed by renovation.

u106-1iba4l0.q: CERCLA is the federal statute that:
c: Created Superfund liability for hazardous-waste cleanup
Sets the 4 pCi/L radon standard as a binding national law
u106-1iba4l0.e: The Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980 created Superfund. Liability is typically strict, joint and several, and retroactive.

u106-i2d289.q: Under CERCLA, a current owner may be required to pay for cleanup even if that owner did not cause the contamination. That is:
c: Liability limited to the down payment
u106-i2d289.e: Strict liability does not require fault. Joint and several liability means one responsible party may be held for the entire cost. Retroactive liability reaches conduct that was legal when it occurred.

u106-1tokzdi.q: The 1986 Superfund amendment that created a stronger innocent-landowner defense is:
u106-1tokzdi.e: SARA (Superfund Amendments and Reauthorization Act) refined CERCLA and recognized defenses for owners who performed appropriate due diligence before purchase.

u106-z6i9wo.q: The usual first environmental due-diligence report, without soil sampling, consists of:
c: Soil borings and laboratory sampling as the first step
Records review, site reconnaissance, and interviews
u106-z6i9wo.e: A Phase I environmental site assessment looks for recognized environmental conditions. If red flags appear, Phase II involves sampling. Lenders and buyers use Phase I to support due-diligence defenses.

u106-6vn181.q: Potentially responsible parties under CERCLA include current owners and operators, past owners at the time of disposal, generators, and:
c: Transporters who selected the disposal site
Listing brokers automatically in every sale
u106-6vn181.e: The statute casts a wide net over parties in the chain of waste handling. An owner who bought after contamination can still be a PRP unless a statutory defense applies.

u106-dpqfa.q: A standard homeowners insurance policy typically does NOT cover:
c: Fire damage from a kitchen accident
Flood damage from a rising river
Theft of personal property inside the dwelling, if the policy so provides
Wind damage from a typical storm, if the policy so provides
u106-dpqfa.e: Flood (and usually earthquake) is excluded from a standard HO policy. Separate flood insurance is written through NFIP or private carriers, and lenders require it in SFHAs.

u106-1ortya7.q: Contaminated sites that are less toxic than Superfund NPL sites and are targeted for reuse are commonly called:
u106-1ortya7.e: Brownfields are abandoned or underused properties with actual or perceived contamination. Federal brownfields policy encourages cleanup and redevelopment.

u106-1e0sl9u.q: Leaking underground storage tanks are an environmental concern because they can:
c: Increase the GRM of nearby rentals
Convert a license into an easement
u106-1e0sl9u.e: USTs that held petroleum or chemicals can leak for years before discovery. Federal UST rules cover many commercial tanks; even exempt residential tanks can be a material disclosure issue.

u106-9q3nk3.q: Urea-formaldehyde foam insulation is a concern because it can release:
u106-9q3nk3.e: UFFI was used in the 1970s and can emit formaldehyde, especially when new. Current emission from old installations is often low, but disclosure of known UFFI is still material.

u106-1uya4zj.q: Carbon monoxide in a dwelling usually comes from:
c: Incomplete combustion of fuel in furnaces, water heaters, or cars in a garage
u106-1uya4zj.e: CO is a colorless, odorless gas. Detectors and proper venting reduce the risk. It is a material safety issue when a faulty appliance is known.

u106-136xzme.q: A seller lists a house as-is. The seller knows the basement floods in every heavy rain. The seller:
c: Need not say anything because as-is waives all disclosure
Must still disclose this known material defect
Must disclose it only to the lender
May disclose it only after the inspection period ends
u106-136xzme.e: As-is allocates repair cost; it does not license concealment of known material facts. Licensees who know of the flooding must disclose it as well.

u106-9e5zjr.q: Mold growth in houses is most closely tied to:
u106-9e5zjr.e: Mold needs moisture. There is no single federal mold-disclosure form, but known, significant mold or chronic leaks are material conditions that should be revealed.

u106-17u0yql.q: A perc test is used to determine whether land can support a:
c: Public sewer tap in a city street
u106-17u0yql.e: A percolation test measures how quickly soil absorbs water. Failed perc can make a lot unbuildable without sewer service and is a material land-use fact.

u106-rehjgz.q: Wetlands filling is commonly regulated at the federal level by the Clean Water Act and permits from:
c: The Army Corps of Engineers (and related EPA authority)
u106-rehjgz.e: Section 404 of the Clean Water Act regulates discharge of dredged or fill material into waters of the United States, including many wetlands. State and local rules may be stricter.

u106-1ing78m.q: An environmental impact statement is most often required for:
c: Major federal actions that significantly affect the environment
Issuance of a certificate of occupancy on a shed
u106-1ing78m.e: NEPA requires federal agencies to study significant environmental effects. Large public projects, not ordinary house sales, trigger EIS practice.

u106-6ubymj.q: A licensee who knows a listed house has a leaking oil tank should:
c: Keep the fact confidential as a seller secret
Disclose it only if the buyer asks a direct question
Disclose the known material environmental condition
Wait until after closing to mention it
u106-6ubymj.e: Known material environmental hazards must be disclosed to the parties. Confidentiality does not cover concealing material defects from a buyer.

u106-3kap0j.q: PCBs are hazardous chemicals historically found in:
c: Electrical transformers and other oil-filled equipment
u106-3kap0j.e: Polychlorinated biphenyls were used in insulating oils. They persist in the environment and can contaminate soil and buildings around old electrical equipment.

u107-wuos7f.q: A seller signs an exclusive right-to-sell listing. During the listing term the seller finds a buyer at a family reunion and closes with no licensee involved. The listing broker is:
c: Owed a commission only if the MLS was used
Owed nothing because the owner procured the buyer
u107-wuos7f.e: Under an exclusive right-to-sell listing the broker is paid if the property sells during the term, even when the owner makes the sale unaided.

u107-p3b59u.q: How does an exclusive-agency listing differ from an exclusive right-to-sell listing?
c: Exclusive agency forbids the listing broker from using the MLS
The owner may sell without paying a commission if the owner finds the buyer without broker help
Exclusive agency pays every broker who showed the property
The listing term is limited by federal law to 30 days
u107-p3b59u.e: Exclusive agency still appoints one broker, but the owner may sell on the owner's own efforts without a fee. Exclusive right-to-sell pays the broker even if the owner finds the buyer.

u107-e1q0gg.q: An owner gives identical open listings to four brokers. The commission is earned by:
c: All four brokers in equal shares
The broker who listed the property first
The broker who is the procuring cause of the sale
Whichever broker the owner prefers after closing
u107-e1q0gg.e: An open listing is a nonexclusive employment. Only the procuring-cause broker is paid, and the owner may sell without a fee.

u107-1eyo3bz.q: The statute of frauds generally requires which of the following to be in writing to be enforceable in court?
c: A six-month lease of a garage
A 90-day contract to work as an unlicensed assistant
A contract for the sale of land
u107-1eyo3bz.e: Contracts for the sale or transfer of an interest in real property must be in writing. Short leases under one year and ordinary employment agreements performable within a year are commonly enforceable even if oral.

u107-efvwai.q: While a paid option to purchase remains unexercised, which party is obligated to complete a sale if the holder elects to buy?
c: Both the optionor and the optionee from day one
Neither party until a deed is delivered
u107-efvwai.e: An option is a unilateral contract: the owner must sell if the holder exercises, but the holder may walk away and forfeit the option money.

u107-1wuvrjy.q: A buyer offers $410,000. The seller replies in writing, "Accepted if you pay $418,000." The seller's reply:
c: Accepts the offer and forms a contract at $410,000
Is a counteroffer that rejects the original offer
Holds the $410,000 offer open for a reasonable time
u107-1wuvrjy.e: Any change in terms is a counteroffer. A counteroffer rejects the original offer, which cannot later be accepted unless the buyer renews it.

u107-59fpfg.q: A seller who is under a valid purchase contract refuses to convey. Because real estate is treated as unique, the buyer may sue for:
c: An automatic doubling of earnest money
A statutory penalty of three times the deposit
u107-59fpfg.e: Specific performance is an equitable remedy that orders the defaulting seller to complete the conveyance. Money damages are also available, but uniqueness of land supports this extra remedy.

u107-1ctb7wy.q: A purchase contract states that if the buyer defaults, the seller may keep the earnest money as the seller's sole remedy. That money is functioning as:
u107-1ctb7wy.e: Liquidated damages are a sum the parties agree in advance will compensate the nonbreaching party. Earnest money often serves that role when the clause is clear and the amount is reasonable.

u107-lakbxs.q: After a purchase contract is signed but before the deed is delivered, the buyer holds:
u107-lakbxs.e: Equitable conversion gives the buyer equitable title (the right to receive the deed). The seller keeps legal title until closing as security for the price.

u107-k4rgfu.q: A contract says "time is of the essence" for the closing date. If one party is not ready to close on that date, the other party may:
c: Ignore the delay because dates in real estate are always flexible
Treat the delay as a material breach and pursue contract remedies
Automatically receive a 30-day extension by law
Record the contract and wait one year
u107-k4rgfu.e: A time-is-of-the-essence clause makes punctual performance a material term. Missing the stated deadline can be a default.

u107-hse3sb.q: A new purchaser is substituted on a contract and the original buyer is fully released from liability. The substitution is:
u107-hse3sb.e: Novation replaces a party or an entire contract and releases the outgoing party. Assignment transfers rights but typically leaves the assignor secondarily liable.

u107-w3vr98.q: A purchase and sale agreement in which the seller promises to convey and the buyer promises to pay is:
u107-w3vr98.e: Each side makes a promise, so the contract is bilateral. A classic option, by contrast, is unilateral until exercised.

u107-1fcubb6.q: A 17-year-old, not emancipated, signs a contract to buy a vacant lot. The contract is:
u107-1fcubb6.e: Contracts of a minor for real estate are voidable by the minor (not by the adult) until a reasonable time after majority, unless a narrow necessity exception applies.

u107-1jdvk7g.q: A purchase contract lets the buyer cancel if a loan commitment is not obtained by a stated date. That provision is:
u107-1jdvk7g.e: A financing contingency makes the buyer's duty to close depend on obtaining the described loan. If the loan is timely denied, the buyer may typically cancel and recover the deposit.

u107-789x8w.q: From the moment of signing until the deed is delivered and the price is paid, a typical purchase contract is:
c: Unenforceable by the statute of limitations
u107-789x8w.e: An executory contract still has material duties outstanding. After closing, when both sides have fully performed, it is executed.

u107-gypbr.q: An offer to buy land, not supported by an option, dies automatically if, before acceptance:
c: The offeree asks a question about the price
The listing broker advertises the property
u107-gypbr.e: Death or insanity of the offeror terminates a revocable offer. An option supported by consideration survives the optionor's death and binds the estate.

u107-ayzo3g.q: Which element is required for a valid real estate contract along with competent parties, lawful purpose, and mutual assent?
u107-ayzo3g.e: Consideration is the bargained-for exchange—usually the price promise and the promise to convey. Recording, appraisals, and attorney signatures are not elements of contract formation.

u107-e34z6k.q: Under an installment land contract (contract for deed), until the buyer pays in full the seller typically retains:
c: Only a lien that must be foreclosed like a mortgage in every state
u107-e34z6k.e: The vendor keeps legal title as security; the vendee holds equitable title and usually possession. The exact foreclosure-like process on default varies by state.

u107-1zlucz.q: After a purchase contract is signed, the parties want to change the closing date. The proper instrument is:
c: A quitclaim from a stranger to the title
An amendment (or modification) of the existing contract
A novation with a third-party lender
u107-1zlucz.e: An amendment changes terms of a contract already in force. An addendum adds terms, usually before or at the time of signing. Both should be signed by the parties.

u107-x6x4w6.q: Earnest money in a purchase contract is:
c: Required for the contract to be valid
Not required for validity; it is evidence of good faith and may serve as liquidated damages
The same thing as consideration for the conveyance
A prepaid commission belonging to the listing broker at once
u107-x6x4w6.e: A contract can be valid without a deposit. The buyer's promise to pay is consideration. Earnest money shows seriousness and is often applied to the price or kept as liquidated damages if so agreed.

u107-1dhug1v.q: An owner promises a neighbor: if the owner decides to sell, the neighbor may match any bona fide third-party offer. The neighbor holds:
c: An option that already binds the owner to sell
A lease with an automatic purchase
u107-1dhug1v.e: A right of first refusal is triggered only if the owner elects to sell. An option lets the holder force a sale during the option term even if the owner does not want to sell.

u107-1j4fghg.q: Both parties to a purchase contract agree in writing to cancel it and return the deposit. This is:
c: A forfeiture declared by one party
u107-1j4fghg.e: Mutual rescission is an agreement to undo the contract and restore the parties, typically returning the earnest money. One party's unilateral cancellation is not rescission.

u107-ps2csf.q: A buyer assigns a purchase contract to a friend. Unless the seller releases the original buyer, the original buyer:
c: Is automatically free of all liability
Usually remains secondarily liable if the assignee defaults
Holds legal title after the assignment
Converts the deal into an option
u107-ps2csf.e: Assignment transfers the assignor's rights. Duties commonly follow, but the assignor stays on the hook unless the seller agrees to a novation.

u107-btm2ag.q: Which of the following is the classic example of a unilateral real estate contract?
c: An option to purchase given for option money
A signed purchase and sale agreement
An exclusive right-to-sell listing with a broker
u107-btm2ag.e: The optionor is bound; the optionee is not bound to buy. Listings, leases, and purchase contracts are typically bilateral because both sides make promises.

u107-13gz951.q: A listing provides that if, within a stated number of days after it expires, the owner sells to a prospect the broker introduced during the term, a commission is still due. That provision is:
u107-13gz951.e: A protection or extender period preserves the broker's fee for a limited time after expiration as to buyers the broker registered or procured, preventing an owner from waiting out the listing.

u108-kw6fr8.q: A lease that begins on June 1 and ends at midnight on May 31 two years later, with no automatic renewal, creates:
c: An estate for years (tenancy for a definite term)
A periodic tenancy from year to year
u108-kw6fr8.e: An estate for years has a fixed start and end, even if the term is not measured in years. No notice is required to end it; it expires on the stated date.

u108-1vppmv0.q: A residential tenancy that automatically continues from period to period until proper notice is given is:
u108-1vppmv0.e: A periodic tenancy (month-to-month or year-to-year) renews by operation of the parties' conduct until one of them gives the notice the lease or law requires.

u108-qyvmun.q: A tenancy that can be ended by either party at any time, often with little or no advance notice beyond what statute requires, is:
u108-qyvmun.e: Tenancy at will lasts only so long as both parties wish. Death of either party or sale of the property typically ends it.

u108-17pnywp.q: After a one-year written lease ends, the occupant remains even though the landlord has refused permission to stay. The occupant's estate is:
c: A periodic tenancy from the first extra day
u108-17pnywp.e: Tenancy at sufferance is a holdover after a lawful estate ends. The landlord may evict or, by accepting rent, may create a new periodic tenancy.

u108-1kx14dy.q: Under a residential gross (straight) lease, the landlord typically pays:
c: Property taxes, insurance, and ordinary operating expenses, while the tenant pays a fixed rent
Nothing; the tenant pays every expense
A percentage of the tenant's retail sales
u108-1kx14dy.e: In a gross lease the stated rent is meant to cover the landlord's usual ownership costs. Net leases shift some or all of those costs to the tenant.

u108-z42nq9.q: A commercial tenant pays a base rent plus property taxes, hazard insurance, and common-area maintenance. The lease is best described as:
c: A ground lease of vacant land only
A percentage lease with no base rent
u108-z42nq9.e: Triple-net leases pass through taxes, insurance, and maintenance. The landlord is left mainly with debt service and perhaps structural items, depending on the form.

u108-hpgtsj.q: A mall shop's rent is a fixed minimum plus a stated percentage of receipts once sales pass a breakpoint. The lease type is:
u108-hpgtsj.e: Percentage leases are common in retail. The overage rent aligns the landlord's return with the tenant's sales.

u108-oodby7.q: A long-term lease of land alone, on which the tenant will construct and own the improvements for the term, is:
u108-oodby7.e: Ground leases are typically long (often decades). Improvements usually revert to the landowner at the end unless the lease says otherwise.

u108-18z3j9t.q: The original tenant transfers every remaining day of the leasehold to a replacement occupant and keeps no reversionary interest. That transfer is:
c: A surrender of the leasehold back to the landlord
An attornment by the original landlord to a mortgagee
u108-18z3j9t.e: Assignment transfers the whole remaining term. A sublease transfers less than the full remaining term, and the original tenant keeps a reversion.

u108-1ks6xdg.q: A landlord refuses for months to repair a broken furnace in winter after repeated notice, making the dwelling unusable. The tenant moves out. The tenant is claiming:
u108-1ks6xdg.e: Constructive eviction occurs when the landlord's wrongful act or omission substantially interferes with use, the tenant gives notice and a chance to cure, and then vacates.

u108-jsybg2.q: A landlord who wants to remove a defaulting tenant through the judicial process is seeking:
u108-jsybg2.e: Actual eviction is the court-supervised removal of the tenant. Self-help lockouts are restricted or forbidden in many jurisdictions.

u108-11ynmhu.q: The covenant of quiet enjoyment promises the tenant that:
c: The premises will be silent after 10 p.m.
No property taxes will ever be levied
Possession will not be disturbed by the landlord or by someone with superior title
u108-11ynmhu.e: Quiet enjoyment is about lawful possession, not noise. The landlord may not harass the tenant or permit a paramount title holder to oust the tenant.

u108-ty1u0m.q: The implied warranty of habitability in residential leases generally requires the landlord to:
c: Keep the dwelling fit for basic living, including essential services and code-level safety
Guarantee the tenant a profit if the tenant sublets
u108-ty1u0m.e: Habitability covers heat, water, sanitation, and other basic living conditions. It cannot usually be waived in a residential lease.

u108-1glagrp.q: A property manager employed to operate an apartment community owes primary fiduciary duties to:
c: Each tenant equally with the owner
u108-1glagrp.e: The management agreement makes the owner the client. Tenants are customers of the operation, not the manager's principals, unless a separate agency is created.

u108-wna2tt.q: The contract that sets a manager's fee, duties, term, and authority to spend and lease is the:
u108-wna2tt.e: A written management agreement is the employment contract between owner and manager. It should state compensation, reports, reserves, and leasing authority.

u108-3gywnp.q: Buying hazard insurance on a managed building is an example of which risk-management technique?
c: Risk avoidance by never owning property
Risk retention by paying every loss from cash
Risk control by installing better locks only
u108-3gywnp.e: Insurance shifts specified financial risk to the insurer in exchange for a premium. Avoidance, retention, and control are the other classic techniques.

u108-1k690d6.q: Under the Americans with Disabilities Act, a property manager of a public accommodation (for example, a retail center) must generally:
c: Make reasonable modifications to policies and remove architectural barriers when that removal is readily achievable
Refuse to rent to anyone who uses a wheelchair because of fire codes
Charge extra rent equal to the cost of any ramp
Ignore federal law if the local code is silent
u108-1k690d6.e: Title III of the ADA covers public accommodations. It requires reasonable modifications of policies, practices, and procedures, and readily achievable barrier removal. Residential dwellings are addressed primarily by the Fair Housing Act.

u108-dy927a.q: Before a tenant signs a lease on a dwelling built before 1978, federal lead-based paint rules require the landlord (or agent) to:
c: Give the EPA pamphlet and disclose known lead-based paint or hazards
Remove all paint of every kind
Test every wall at the landlord's expense in all cases
u108-dy927a.e: Target housing (pre-1978) requires disclosure of known information, an EPA-approved pamphlet, and a chance to inspect. It does not require the owner to abate in every rental.

u108-68ugd4.q: An owner sells a warehouse and immediately rents it back from the buyer to continue operations. The arrangement is:
c: A ground lease of vacant land
u108-68ugd4.e: A sale-leaseback frees capital for the seller-tenant while the buyer-landlord receives a long-term rental stream. The seller becomes a tenant.

u108-o2969t.q: A commercial lease that adjusts rent by reference to a published cost-of-living index is:
c: A gross lease with no adjustments
u108-o2969t.e: Index leases keep the landlord's real return closer to inflation. The index, adjustment dates, and any cap should be spelled out.

u108-1xgw8sw.q: A clause that raises commercial rent to pass through increases in taxes or operating costs is:
u108-1xgw8sw.e: Escalation or expense-stop clauses shift specified cost increases to the tenant so the landlord's net is more stable.

u108-4qzu7a.q: A lease that starts at a lower rent and has scheduled increases at set intervals is:
c: A pure percentage lease with no base rent
A ground lease of land only
u108-4qzu7a.e: Graduated leases use predetermined bumps, often to help a new business ramp up. They differ from index leases, which float with an outside index.

u108-1r6eweh.q: Security deposits collected from residential tenants should be treated as:
c: The landlord's unrestricted operating cash on the day received
The tenant's money, held according to law and applied only to unpaid rent or documented damage
A nonrefundable fee in every state
Commission belonging to the leasing agent
u108-1r6eweh.e: A security deposit is not rent in advance. It remains the tenant's funds, subject to statutory handling, accounting, and return rules that vary by state.

u108-1te97gd.q: In an office building, usable square footage is the space a tenant actually occupies. Rentable square footage typically also includes:
c: A proportionate share of common areas such as lobbies and corridors
u108-1te97gd.e: Rentable area equals usable area plus the tenant's share of corridors, restrooms, and lobby. A load or add-on factor converts usable feet into the rentable feet used to compute rent.

u108-2rb0m.q: If a landlord accepts rent after a lease expires and the parties do not sign a new term, the holdover often becomes:
u108-2rb0m.e: Acceptance of rent after expiration commonly creates a month-to-month (or other periodic) tenancy on the old terms, except those that conflict with a periodic estate.

u109-gjdkyw.q: The deed that usually contains the full set of covenants (seisin, right to convey, against encumbrances, quiet enjoyment, further assurance, and warranty forever) is a:
c: Sheriff's deed after a tax sale
u109-gjdkyw.e: A general warranty deed warrants title against defects arising both before and during the grantor's ownership. It gives the grantee the most deed-based protection.

u109-eckdcg.q: A special warranty deed typically warrants title against defects that:
c: Arose during the grantor's period of ownership
Arose at any time in the chain of title
The grantor has never heard of
Only a title insurer may raise
u109-eckdcg.e: Special (limited) warranty covers only claims arising by, through, or under the grantor. Earlier defects are not warranted by that grantor.

c: A full warranty of marketable title
An implied covenant of seisin in every state
Whatever interest the grantor actually has, with no title covenants
A new fee simple even if the grantor owns nothing
u109-8ox8pu.e: Quitclaim deeds are used to clear clouds and to transfer uncertain interests. If the grantor owns nothing, the grantee receives nothing.

u109-zkqiwm.q: For a deed to transfer title, it must be delivered to and accepted by the grantee during the grantor's lifetime (or by valid escrow). Delivery is primarily a question of:
c: The county clerk's filing stamp alone
Whether the deed was drafted on a statutory form
Whether the grantor intended to pass title
u109-zkqiwm.e: Intent to make a present transfer is the heart of delivery. Recording is not required for validity between the parties, though it is essential for protection against later purchasers.

u109-141ft8h.q: Acknowledgment of a deed (notarization of the grantor's signature) is required primarily so that the deed can be:
c: Valid between grantor and grantee in every case
Recorded in the public land records
u109-141ft8h.e: Between the parties, an unacknowledged deed may still pass title if delivered. Recording statutes generally require acknowledgment (or a substitute) before the clerk will accept the instrument.

u109-6iaxrb.q: An owner's title insurance policy, once issued, typically remains in force:
c: For as long as the owner or the owner's heirs have an interest, up to the policy amount
Only until the first property-tax bill
For one year, like a hazard policy
Only while a mortgage remains unpaid
u109-6iaxrb.e: Owner's coverage is a one-time premium that protects the named insured and usually the insured's heirs for as long as they hold an interest. A lender's policy declines as the loan is paid and ends when the loan is satisfied.

c: The borrower against every title defect without a deductible
The lender, generally up to the outstanding loan balance
u109-11kidxc.e: The mortgagee policy insures the lien's priority and validity. The face amount typically tracks the loan and shrinks as principal is paid.

u109-1djf83b.q: A condensed chronological history of recorded instruments affecting a parcel, prepared by an abstractor, is:
c: A Torrens certificate in every state
u109-1djf83b.e: An abstract summarizes the public record. An attorney or title examiner then issues an opinion; title insurance is a separate contract of indemnity.

u109-qlfb4d.q: A gap, forgery, or undisclosed heir that makes ownership uncertain is commonly called:
u109-qlfb4d.e: A cloud is any claim or defect that impairs marketability. It may be removed by a quitclaim, a release, or a quiet-title action.

u109-ma037l.q: Recording a deed in the county land records gives the world:
c: Constructive notice of the recorded interest
Actual notice only to people who were at closing
Inquiry notice only if the deed is unacknowledged
u109-ma037l.e: Constructive notice is the law's presumption that a person knows what the public records would reveal. Actual notice is what a person really knows.

u109-51g3nb.q: In a race-notice recording state, a later bona fide purchaser prevails against a prior unrecorded deed only if the later purchaser:
c: Takes with actual knowledge of the prior deed
Is a donee who paid nothing
Takes without notice and records first
u109-51g3nb.e: Race-notice protects a subsequent purchaser for value who lacks notice of the prior claim and who records before that prior claim is recorded.

u109-n19fzg.q: Under the federal TRID rules, a lender must generally provide the Closing Disclosure to the borrower at least:
c: On the day of closing only
u109-n19fzg.e: The Closing Disclosure must arrive at least three business days before consummation so the borrower can review cash-to-close, the APR, and other terms. Certain last-minute changes restart the wait.

u109-165nax5.q: At closing, prepaid but unused property taxes that the seller already paid are typically:
c: A credit to the seller and a debit to the buyer
A debit to the seller and a credit to the buyer
u109-165nax5.e: The buyer will enjoy the prepaid period after closing, so the buyer reimburses the seller. Unpaid taxes that cover the seller's period run the opposite way.

u109-1sma9hq.q: Which closing cost is customarily a buyer expense on a financed purchase (practice may vary by local custom)?
c: The loan origination fee and the lender's title policy
The brokerage commission specified in the listing
Unpaid property taxes for the seller's period of ownership
u109-1sma9hq.e: Buyers typically pay their loan fees and the mortgagee title policy. Sellers typically pay the listing commission and often a transfer tax, subject to contract and local custom.

c: Has no recorded history at all
Is insured for more than the price
A reasonably well-informed buyer would accept as free from serious defects and litigation risk
Has been held for at least 99 years
u109-dpq960.e: Marketable title need not be perfect, but it must not expose the buyer to a reasonable threat of litigation or to substantial defects. A purchase contract usually requires it.

u109-15k8iom.q: A lawsuit brought to remove a cloud and confirm ownership against adverse claimants is:
c: A partition action among spouses only
An interpleader of earnest money only
u109-15k8iom.e: Quiet title names possible claimants, gives them a chance to appear, and produces a decree that settles the record. It is a common cure for clouds that deeds will not clear.

u109-36havq.q: Closing through a disinterested third party who holds funds and documents until all conditions occur is:
u109-36havq.e: In escrow, the escrow holder is a dual agent with limited, written instructions. When the conditions are met, the holder records the deed and disburses funds.

u109-8ns9e7.q: To be a valid grantor of a deed, a person must generally:
c: Be legally competent and sign the deed
Be the same age as the grantee
Have title insurance already in force
u109-8ns9e7.e: The grantor must be identifiable, competent, and must sign. The grantee must be identifiable and capable of taking title but does not sign a typical warranty deed.

u109-1xetkwm.q: At or before closing, which settlement practice does RESPA Section 8 make illegal?
c: A borrower independently shopping among competing title companies
Kickbacks and unearned fees for settlement-service referrals on covered federally related loans
The use of a Closing Disclosure
u109-1xetkwm.e: Section 8 bars giving or accepting a thing of value for the referral of settlement business. Affiliated-business disclosures and bona fide payments for actual services are the lawful path.

u109-ird36x.q: The habendum clause in a deed is the clause that typically begins:
c: "To have and to hold" and describes the estate granted
"Know all persons by these presents" only
u109-ird36x.e: The granting clause transfers the interest; the habendum ("to have and to hold") describes the estate (for example, in fee simple). If they conflict, the granting clause usually controls.

u109-fosx3o.q: A complete successive list of conveyances and encumbrances from a starting point (often a patent or an agreed root) down to the present owner is the:
u109-fosx3o.e: The chain of title is the linked series of owners. A gap in the chain, or a stray deed out of the chain, is a classic cloud.

u109-5tyf45.q: Real property passing to heirs when the owner dies without a valid will passes by:
c: Escheat in every case, even if heirs exist
u109-5tyf45.e: Descent is the statutory scheme for intestacy. A devise is a gift of real property by will. Escheat applies only when no eligible heir exists.

u109-n26sh8.q: Title to a refrigerator that is personal property (not a fixture) is transferred at closing by:
c: A general warranty deed covering the land only
u109-n26sh8.e: Deeds convey real property. A bill of sale conveys personal property. Whether an appliance is a fixture depends on annexation, intent, and adaptation.

u109-19em19h.q: A buyer who inspects the property and sees a tenant in possession is charged with:
c: No notice of the tenant's rights
Constructive notice from the deed records only
Actual notice of the occupancy, and inquiry notice of the tenant's claimed interest
u109-19em19h.e: Possession is notice. A prudent buyer must ask what rights the occupant claims. Recording statutes do not erase interests a visit would reveal.

u109-1v0xogo.q: Adverse possession generally requires possession that is open, notorious, exclusive, hostile, and continuous for the statutory period. "Hostile" in this setting means:
c: The possessor physically assaulted the owner
The possessor had the owner's written permission
The possession is without the owner's permission and inconsistent with the owner's title
u109-1v0xogo.e: Hostile means a claim contrary to the true owner's rights, not personal anger. Permission (a lease or license) defeats hostility.

u110-14p41t0.q: Which class is protected by the federal Fair Housing Act but is not a basis of the Civil Rights Act of 1866?
u110-14p41t0.e: The 1866 Act reaches racial discrimination in property. The Fair Housing Act of 1968 added religion and national origin (and later sex, disability, and familial status).

u110-1r371ni.q: The Civil Rights Act of 1866 prohibits discrimination in the sale or rental of property on the basis of:
c: Race and color, with no housing exemptions
u110-1r371ni.e: Jones v. Mayer confirmed that the 1866 Act bars all racial discrimination in property, public or private. Fair Housing Act exemptions do not limit the 1866 Act.

u110-166t9l8.q: A licensee shows families with children only houses near schools and shows childless couples only downtown lofts, based on those family facts. This is:
u110-166t9l8.e: Steering is directing people toward or away from neighborhoods or buildings because of a protected class. Clients may state their own preferences; the agent may not channel them by class.

u110-tpsi9e.q: An agent tells owners, "Sell now—a different racial group is moving in and prices will drop." The agent is engaging in:
u110-tpsi9e.e: Blockbusting is inducing listings or sales by exploiting prejudice or fear of demographic change. It is illegal under the Fair Housing Act.

u110-1a0psrt.q: A lender refuses to make loans in a mixed-race neighborhood regardless of each applicant's credit. This is:
u110-1a0psrt.e: Redlining is denying credit or insurance based on the demographics of a geographic area rather than on the applicant and the collateral.

u110-1fhfu1b.q: In Jones v. Alfred H. Mayer Co., the Supreme Court held that the Civil Rights Act of 1866:
c: Bans racial discrimination in private property transactions
Was repealed by the Fair Housing Act
u110-1fhfu1b.e: Jones v. Mayer (1968) read 42 U.S.C. § 1982 to prohibit all racial discrimination in the sale or rental of property, including purely private deals.

u110-9c4ovo.q: The Fair Housing Amendments Act of 1988 added which protected classes?
u110-9c4ovo.e: Federal fair housing now covers race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, and disability. Age, occupation, and source of income are not federal FHA classes (they may be under other laws or local ordinances).

u110-bc2gzz.q: Competing brokerage firms agree that all residential listings will be taken at 6 percent. This agreement is:
c: Illegal price-fixing under the Sherman Antitrust Act
u110-bc2gzz.e: Commission rates must be independently set by each firm and negotiated with the client. An agreement among competitors on fees is per se price-fixing.

u110-1asdp4y.q: All but one of the brokerages in a town jointly decide to withhold MLS cooperation from a firm that advertises discounted fees. The agreement is:
c: Required by MLS bylaws in every market
A tie-in arrangement with a title company
u110-1asdp4y.e: A group boycott is concerted refusal to deal with a competitor. Each firm may independently choose its own business model; they may not combine to punish another firm.

u110-1gm5nab.q: Two competing firms secretly divide the county: one will handle only luxury listings and the other only first-time buyers. This is:
u110-1gm5nab.e: Dividing geographic markets or customer types among competitors suppresses competition and violates the Sherman Act.

u110-ufygfj.q: A listing broker tells a seller, "I will take the listing only if you agree to buy your home-warranty policy from my affiliate." This is:
c: A lawful package sale in every case
An illegal tying (tie-in) arrangement when used to force the extra product
u110-ufygfj.e: Tie-in arrangements condition the desired service on the purchase of a second product. The seller must be free to choose settlement providers, subject to lawful affiliated-business disclosures.

u110-pdduuf.q: A broker deposits a buyer's earnest-money check into the broker's general operating account. This is:
c: Conversion of the funds to the broker's use
Proper if the deal is expected to close
Required so the broker can pay bills
u110-pdduuf.e: Commingling is mixing client or customer funds with the broker's own money. Conversion is the next step: actually using those funds.

u110-b2pi8i.q: A broker pays the office rent with money from a client's earnest-money trust account. This is:
c: Commingling only, because the check still cleared
Required if the operating account is overdrawn
u110-b2pi8i.e: Conversion is the misappropriation of funds belonging to another. It is grounds for loss of license and may be a crime.

u110-t3hk5r.q: Dual agency, where one firm represents both seller and buyer in the same transaction, generally requires:
c: No disclosure if the commission is split
Informed written consent of both parties (as required by applicable agency law)
u110-t3hk5r.e: Undisclosed dual agency is a breach of fiduciary duty. Informed consent, typically in writing, is the usual legal path; some states restrict or forbid dual agency.

u110-1kjy0yz.q: Loyalty as a fiduciary duty requires the agent to:
c: Guarantee that the property will appraise
Put the client's interests above the agent's and above others' in the transaction
Keep every fact secret from the client
u110-1kjy0yz.e: OLD CAR / COALD duties include obedience (to lawful instructions), loyalty, disclosure, confidentiality, accounting, and reasonable care. Loyalty means the client's interest comes first.

u110-s2n33t.q: Federal tax rules generally treat a real estate salesperson as an independent contractor when the salesperson:
c: Must keep set office hours and is paid an hourly wage
Is forbidden in every case from any other employment even off duty
Receives employee health insurance as the only compensation
Is licensed, is paid chiefly by commission, and has a written independent-contractor agreement
u110-s2n33t.e: A salesperson is a statutory nonemployee for federal tax purposes if licensed, paid chiefly on output rather than hours, and working under a written independent-contractor agreement. The broker must still supervise licensed activity.

u110-1kssf0a.q: A seller's agent says, "This is the most charming cottage on the block." That statement is best classified as:
c: Puffing (opinion or exaggeration not meant as fact)
Fraudulent concealment of a latent defect
A trigger term under Regulation Z
u110-1kssf0a.e: Puffing is subjective opinion. It becomes misrepresentation when it states a material fact that is false or when it conceals a known defect.

u110-1f5tbnw.q: A hidden structural defect that a reasonably careful visual inspection would not reveal, and that the seller knows about, is:
c: A patent defect the buyer must discover unaided
A latent defect that generally must be disclosed
u110-1f5tbnw.e: Latent defects are not obvious. Sellers and their agents must disclose known material latent defects; patent defects are visible and the buyer can see them.

u110-1uczegw.q: Federal lead-based paint rules give a buyer of target housing (pre-1978) a period of how many days to conduct a paint inspection or risk assessment, unless the parties agree otherwise?
c: One business day with no waiver
Ninety days that cannot be shortened
None; inspection is forbidden until after closing
u110-1uczegw.e: The buyer must receive a 10-day opportunity (or another agreed period) to inspect. The buyer may waive it. Disclosure of known lead hazards is still required.

u110-1m4o0d7.q: The federal Do Not Call rules generally allow a licensee to call a consumer whose number is on the registry if the licensee has an established business relationship, for up to:
c: 18 months after the last transaction (and 3 months after an inquiry)
Ten years after any website visit
u110-1m4o0d7.e: An established business relationship permits calls for 18 months after a purchase or transaction and 3 months after an inquiry. The consumer may still demand no further calls.

u110-1ljlqhe.q: The Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA) makes it unlawful for a creditor to discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age (with limited exceptions), or because the applicant:
c: Receives income from a public-assistance program
Wants a larger loan than the collateral supports
Refuses to provide a Social Security number
u110-1ljlqhe.e: ECOA protects the credit-application process. Public-assistance income cannot be discounted because of its source. Creditworthiness may still be considered.

u110-gdxr7h.q: Under TILA/Regulation Z advertising rules, if a licensee's ad states a triggering term such as the amount of a monthly payment, the ad must also state:
c: A slogan approved by the MLS
The APR and other required credit terms
u110-gdxr7h.e: General statements such as "easy financing" do not trigger full disclosure. Specific terms (down payment, payment amount, number of payments, or finance charge) do, and the APR must appear.

u110-1z0fbuy.q: In designated (appointed) agency within one firm, the broker typically:
c: Must keep both files in a single shared folder with no walls
Acts as a dual agent for every in-house deal automatically
Appoints separate licensees to represent the seller and the buyer, with information barriers
u110-1z0fbuy.e: Designated agency lets one firm give each party a dedicated agent. The broker remains responsible for supervision and for protecting confidential information.

u110-ey00i5.q: Client funds held by a broker must be placed in a trust (escrow) account that is:
c: Combined with the brokerage operating account each Friday
Used to pay unlicensed assistants first
Separate from the broker's operating and personal funds
u110-ey00i5.e: A trust account is a fiduciary account, usually demand-deposit and federally insured, used only for other people's money. Mixing or using those funds is commingling or conversion.

u110-ehbgfo.q: A material false statement of fact that a buyer relies on to purchase, made by an agent who knew it was false, is:
u110-ehbgfo.e: Fraud requires a false material fact, knowledge or reckless disregard, intent that the other party rely, actual reliance, and damage. Innocent misrepresentation can still support rescission without the intent element.

u111-1r2ak7a.q: A $420,000 closing generates a 6% brokerage fee. The listing office and selling office split the fee 50/50. The listing salesperson is on a 60% split with the listing office. The listing salesperson's share is:
u111-1r2ak7a.e: Total commission is $420,000 × 0.06 = $25,200. The listing side is one-half, or $12,600. Sixty percent of $12,600 is $7,560.

u111-kg54jp.q: A rectangular parcel measures 220 feet by 396 feet. How many acres does it contain?
u111-kg54jp.e: 220 × 396 = 87,120 square feet. One acre is 43,560 square feet, so 87,120 ÷ 43,560 = 2 acres.

u111-15wcr47.q: A lender charges 2 discount points on a $180,000 loan. The cost of the points is:
u111-15wcr47.e: One point is 1% of the loan amount. Two points = 0.02 × $180,000 = $3,600, paid in cash at closing unless financed.

u111-s64ajt.q: A $200,000 loan bears 6% annual interest. Using a 360-day year and a 30-day month, the interest for one month is:
u111-s64ajt.e: Annual interest is $200,000 × 0.06 = $12,000. One 30-day month is 30/360 = 1/12 of the year, so $12,000 ÷ 12 = $1,000.

u111-10m86bn.q: Calendar-year taxes of $3,600 were prepaid by the seller. Closing is July 31; the seller owns the day of closing. Using a 360-day year (12 months of 30 days), the tax proration is a credit to the seller of:
u111-10m86bn.e: Daily rate = $3,600 ÷ 360 = $10. The seller used January–July (7 × 30 = 210 days). Unused days remaining for the buyer: 360 − 210 = 150. Credit to seller = 150 × $10 = $1,500 (or 5/12 × $3,600).

u111-k10sw1.q: A fourplex sells for $360,000. Monthly gross rent is $2,000. The monthly gross rent multiplier (GRM) is:
u111-k10sw1.e: Monthly GRM = sale price ÷ monthly rent = $360,000 ÷ $2,000 = 180.

u111-1xhxsk0.q: Residential rental property is depreciated for federal tax purposes over 27.5 years using straight line. If the building (improvements only) is worth $275,000, the annual depreciation deduction is:
u111-1xhxsk0.e: $275,000 ÷ 27.5 = $10,000 per year. Land is not depreciated; only the improvement basis is divided by 27.5 years.

u111-hdeomq.q: A property is assessed at $180,000. The tax rate is 25 mills. The annual property tax is:
u111-hdeomq.e: A mill is $1 per $1,000 of assessed value, so 25 mills = 0.025. Tax = $180,000 × 0.025 = $4,500.

u111-nt9tn6.e: Daily rent = $1,800 ÷ 30 = $60. The seller keeps 11 days ($660). The buyer is credited for the remaining 19 days: 19 × $60 = $1,140.

u111-1wi1kjc.e: GRM = $240,000 ÷ $1,500 = 160. Using that GRM, a similar house renting for $1,600 per month would indicate $256,000.

u111-1n21zzf.q: Nonresidential real property is depreciated over 39 years straight line. If the building basis is $390,000, annual depreciation is:
u111-1n21zzf.e: $390,000 ÷ 39 = $10,000 per year. Residential rental improvements use 27.5 years; land is never depreciated.
