u111-muy9ch.q: A buyer is obtaining a 90% LTV loan on a $320,000 purchase and will pay 1.5 points. The dollar amount of the points is:
u111-muy9ch.e: Loan = 0.90 × $320,000 = $288,000. Points = 0.015 × $288,000 = $4,320. Points are computed on the loan, not on the price.

g1-12fsica.d: The part of the NY Real Property Law that governs licensing of real estate brokers and salespersons (§440–§443-a).

g1-kmya38.d: Someone who, for another and for a fee, lists, sells, buys, exchanges, rents, negotiates or collects rent for real estate (RPL §440).

g1-1m6kzkg.d: A licensed broker who chooses to work under another broker's name and supervision; practices under the rules for salespersons.

g1-10e5o3i.d: A licensee associated with (sponsored by) a broker who performs brokerage activities on the broker's behalf.

g1-156bs6d.d: The DOS-issued ID card with the licensee's photo, name, business address and broker's name; must be shown on demand.

g1-vvmexp.d: Moving a salesperson's license to a new sponsoring broker. The new broker files a record of association ($20).

g1-qd4o9l.d: Mixing a client's money with the broker's own funds. Prohibited (19 NYCRR 175.1).

g1-1d5q8ns.d: Money or documents held by a neutral party until conditions are met. Brokers must deposit client funds within 3 business days.

g1-1tulgx2.d: A listing where the broker keeps everything over a set net price to the seller. Illegal in NY.

g1-1ot5903.d: An ad that doesn't disclose that the advertiser is a real estate broker. Prohibited.

g1-eirl88.d: An undisclosed payment for a referral or business. Prohibited under RESPA and NY rules.

g1-8fzah9.d: A nonresident licensee's filing that appoints the NY Secretary of State to accept legal process on their behalf.

g1-19zact4.d: A court proceeding to review decisions of state and local agencies, such as DOS or a ZBA.

g1-1djvhi1.d: A crime less serious than a felony. Unlicensed activity or any violation of Article 12-A is a misdemeanor.

g1-151dwr1.d: DOS action against a licensee: revocation, suspension, a fine up to $2,000, or a reprimand.

g1-1w1jhb3.d: 22.5 hours per 2-year term, including fair housing, implicit bias, cultural competency, ethics, legal updates and agency.

g1-m9vtl1.d: A person licensed by DOS who, for a fee, provides information about available rentals.

g1-pmqrik.d: A person licensed by DOS who, for a fee, arranges shared living accommodations (roommates).

g1-gcat89.d: A cooperative system through which brokers share listings.

g1-v3zt07.d: A contract between an owner and a broker authorizing the broker to market the property.

g1-zddyd.d: A professional licensed under RPL Article 12-B who inspects the condition of residential property.

g1-xm7mv2.d: The seller's disclosure form required for 1–4 family home sales before the buyer signs a contract. The $500 credit option ended 3/20/2024.

g1-1vai8gf.d: Property associated with a death, crime or disease. Under RPL §443-a, such facts aren't material defects in NY.

g1-7bi7ah.d: A support person who may do clerical tasks but may not show property, host open houses or negotiate.

g2-3k1bg4.d: A person authorized to act on behalf of another (the principal).

g2-4igmq7.d: The person who hires and is represented by an agent; the client.

g2-1bqb0is.d: The party an agent represents and owes fiduciary duties to.

g2-152aas7.d: A third party the agent deals with but doesn't represent; owed honesty and fair dealing.

g2-1pbw04l.d: A person in a position of trust who must act in the principal's best interest.

g2-1ges6j7.d: Reasonable care, undivided loyalty, confidentiality, full disclosure, obedience and duty to account.

g2-wob767.d: The duty to put the client's interests above everyone else's, including the agent's own.

g2-19vniar.d: The duty to follow the principal's lawful instructions.

g2-kiixif.d: The duty to safeguard and account for all money and property of the principal.

g2-1qtsyu4.d: The duty to use the skill and diligence of a competent licensee.

g2-vn3x1p.d: An agent authorized to do anything the principal could do, as under a general power of attorney.

g2-1ndqxea.d: An agent authorized to handle a range of matters in one area, e.g., a property manager.

g2-1nzobhx.d: An agent authorized for one specific task, e.g., a listing broker.

g2-d2et4u.d: An agent of an agent. For example, a cooperating broker working for the seller through the listing broker.

g2-1yk5ar7.d: A cooperating agent engaged by the listing or buyer's agent (not the client). The client has no vicarious liability for them.

g2-11yw6bm.d: One broker representing both buyer and seller (or tenant and landlord) in the same transaction. Requires informed written consent of both.

g2-1cx4078.d: A salesperson assigned by a dual-agent broker to advocate for one party. They still cannot give undivided loyalty.

g2-8v91o1.d: Written informed consent, given ahead of time on the §443 form, to possible dual agency.

g2-gmet33.d: Representing both sides without informed written consent. Illegal.

g2-u8yekz.d: Agreement given after full explanation of the relationship and its consequences.

g2-17rawp2.d: Agency created by an oral or written agreement.

g2-1or3u80.d: Agency created by the conduct of the parties.

g2-1l08kbm.d: Approving an agent's unauthorized act after the fact, creating agency.

g2-1myyt8x.d: When a principal's conduct led a third party to believe an agency existed, the principal can't deny it.

g2-23bo4d.d: Liability of a principal for the acts of its agent or subagent.

g2-1jzfnlt.d: A false statement or concealment of a material fact. It can be intentional (fraud) or negligent.

g2-za98xc.d: An agent acting for personal gain at the client's expense, e.g., secretly buying the listing.

g2-akkh4h.d: The first meeting or conversation that goes beyond general chat into specifics. It triggers the §443 disclosure.

g2-1j5j3wt.d: The RPL §443 form explaining agency relationships in residential sales and rentals. It states it is "not a contract."

g2-1jik832.d: A listing that pays the broker no matter who finds the buyer, even the owner.

g2-og86fo.d: A listing that pays the broker unless the owner finds the buyer personally.

g2-vd7029.d: A non-exclusive listing. Only the broker who is the procuring cause is paid.

g2-11jgdp9.d: Competitors agreeing on commission rates. An antitrust violation.

g2-1t6dp6e.d: Competitors agreeing not to deal with another firm. An antitrust violation.

g2-13brofj.d: Competitors dividing territories or customers. An antitrust violation.

g2-11y3rpb.d: Requiring the purchase of one product or service as a condition of getting another. An antitrust violation.

g2-osv38y.d: A worker paid by results who controls how the work is done. Most salespeople, under a written contract (IRC §3508).

g2-1y8f17p.d: A worker whose employer directs and controls the work. The employer owes payroll taxes, workers' comp and unemployment insurance.

g3-5og3z9.d: The ownership rights of possession, control, enjoyment, exclusion and disposition.

g3-19qxm7i.d: Land, permanent improvements and the bundle of legal rights of ownership.

g3-8rw738.d: Movable property not attached to land.

g3-3u8pkc.d: Personal property attached to real estate so that it becomes part of the real property.

g3-11ldk9o.d: An item a commercial tenant installs for business. It remains the tenant's property and is removable before the lease ends.

g3-1st2aqa.d: The right to use the space above the surface of land.

g3-xb7ww9.d: Rights to the area below the surface, such as minerals.

g3-1pc68i4.d: Rights of owners along flowing water (rivers, streams).

g3-19p8wdd.d: Rights of owners along lakes, seas and oceans.

g3-1fegi2l.d: The gradual addition of land by natural deposits of soil (alluvion).

g3-3hiyom.d: The sudden loss of land by natural force. The owner keeps title to the original boundary.

g3-xnw29x.d: The most complete ownership. It lasts indefinitely and is inheritable.

g3-q3ssiz.d: Ownership that lasts for someone's lifetime.

g3-1nwbah8.d: The future interest of a third party who takes the property when a life estate ends.

g3-vm1zjw.d: The grantor's future right to get the property back when an estate ends.

g3-cix4xi.d: Damage or neglect by a life tenant that harms the future interest.

g3-4ajkl2.d: A leasehold with a definite beginning and end.

g3-pff1hg.d: Ownership by one person or entity alone.

g3-zmx5zr.d: Co-ownership with undivided, possibly unequal shares and no right of survivorship.

g3-citttn.d: Co-ownership with the four unities (time, title, interest, possession) and a right of survivorship.

g3-18rhqg7.d: Co-ownership by married spouses with survivorship. It can't be severed by one spouse alone.

g3-ecpyyk.d: The surviving co-owner(s) automatically take a deceased co-owner's share.

g3-4qq8pb.d: Each co-owner's right to possess the whole property, rather than a specific part.

g3-gjr13z.d: A court action to divide co-owned property or order its sale.

g3-t5erhg.d: Historic life-estate rights of a surviving husband or wife. Abolished in NY.

g3-1q7avtr.d: Protection of some equity in a primary residence from certain creditors.

g3-1nkcs6a.d: Property passing to the state when the owner dies without a will or heirs.

g3-16e12eb.d: The trustee holds title for a beneficiary. The trustor (settlor) creates the trust.

g3-1lxj5mu.d: The person who benefits from a trust or will.

g3-1j91x1u.d: Two or more parties joining for a single project.

g3-n6rxew.d: Any claim or restriction that lessens the value or use of property: liens, easements, restrictions, encroachments.

g3-yjxfn1.d: A claim against property as security for a debt.

g3-knaa7c.d: A general lien attaches to all of a debtor's property (a judgment). A specific lien attaches to one property (a mortgage, tax lien).

g3-18qfdiz.d: Involuntary liens are imposed by law (taxes, judgments). Voluntary liens are created by the owner (a mortgage).

g3-1p7u0yn.d: A lien filed by an unpaid contractor or supplier for improvements: generally within 8 months, or 4 months for a single-family home.

g3-1aqu122.d: A recorded notice of a pending lawsuit affecting title.

g3-1hovdq.d: An agreement that changes lien priority, making one lien junior to another.

g3-sts047.d: A non-possessory right to use another's land for a specific purpose.

g3-o0z615.d: An easement that benefits a neighboring parcel and runs with the land.

g3-zhe1ks.d: An easement benefiting a person or company (like a utility), with no dominant parcel.

g3-rxhh9b.d: The parcel that benefits from an easement.

g3-1uauy1h.d: The parcel burdened by an easement.

g3-ykfcp5.d: An easement for access to a landlocked parcel.

g3-nwrdys.d: An easement acquired by open, notorious, continuous, hostile use for 10 years in NY.

g3-1y7j1pt.d: An easement acquired by the government through eminent domain.

g3-1llrv1h.d: A shared wall on the boundary between two properties.

g3-lp35xr.d: Personal, revocable permission to use land. Not an interest in land.

g3-1m45qrg.d: An improvement that extends onto a neighbor's property.

g3-ro9qx5.d: An easement allowing passage over another's land.

g3-yjr6fr.d: A written instrument that conveys title to real property.

g3-1yqpkif.d: The grantor conveys the property; the grantee receives it.

g3-1uk8qg6.d: The deed clause ("to have and to hold") that defines the estate granted.

g3-36meqf.d: Something of value exchanged. It is recited in deeds and required in contracts.

g3-uq04s8.d: A formal declaration before a notary that a signature is voluntary. Required to record a deed.

g3-k2rwxv.d: The steps that pass title under a deed.

g3-1x73eib.d: The deed with the most protection: seizin, quiet enjoyment, against encumbrances, further assurances, warranty.

g3-ok9wir.d: A deed implying the grantor holds title. It may include a covenant against the grantor's own acts.

g3-qvsaao.d: A deed conveying whatever interest the grantor has, with no warranties.

g3-f5srov.d: A deed given by a court-appointed referee, e.g., after a foreclosure sale.

g3-568p6p.d: A legal description using a point of beginning, directions and distances, and monuments.

roadmap.title: Take the 77-hour course (it can be free)
roadmap.next: Enroll in the free 77-hour course at LearnCycle (the "License Essentials" tier) and start the first module.

roadmap.title: Get your New York photo ID
roadmap.next: Moved here recently? Swap your out-of-state license at the DMV (New York asks new residents to do it within 30 days).

roadmap.title: Pass the school's final exam (proctored)
roadmap.next: Book an approved proctor for your course final. Call your local library first; many do it free.

roadmap.title: Schedule the state exam on eAccessNY
roadmap.next: Make your eAccessNY account and book the $15 state exam once your mock scores reach 80%.

roadmap.title: Pass, then find a sponsoring broker
roadmap.next: Pass the state exam, then line up a sponsoring broker. Interview a few.

roadmap.title: Apply for the license
roadmap.next: Apply for your license in eAccessNY ($65); your broker approves it online.

roadmap.title: After you're licensed
roadmap.next: You're licensed. Renew every 2 years with 22.5 hours of continuing education.
